📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There were massive changes at the Pilot Field in the summer, with Wood taking on the role of head of football and Ronnie Dolan appointed first-team manager.

Dolan, his right-hand men Sam Adams and Trevor McCreadie and a reshaped squad got off to a flying start in the league but have hit a rough run of results – most recently last Saturday’s 4-1 home loss to Steyning, which came after they led 1-0 at the break.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

But Wood said everyone at the club was committed to making a success of the season – not just for the men’s team but for United’s women and the younger teams too.

Wood noted of the Isthmian South East promotion bid: “We have to be challenging for the play-offs, as a minimum.

"The primary objective is to reach the last day of the season with the title to play for, or already won, or a play-off place to secure or in the bag. Mid-table would be a failure.”.

Wood said those in charge at the Pilot Field were working to get the club’s local identity back after a couple of years when it had drifted alongside the team dropping from step three to step four.

He noted these efforts were reflected in the type of players they had recruited and added: “We’ve wanted to bring in players whose character fits the club. We want people here long-term – we don’t want a revolving door.

In a recent development, "As for the season so far, we’re up there challenging. We’ve hit a sticky patch but every team does that. Everyone’s learning – it’s Ronnie’s first job as a manager and many of the players are very young.”.

On that note, Wood said the club’s ‘pathway’ was beginning to bear fruit, and he praised the younger teams’ coaches for developing some highly promising talent. Some are knocking on the first-team squad’s door – others are being loaned out to step five clubs.

The under-18s in particular are going well, Wood remarked: “They include so many young players who will enrich local football in years to come.”.

According to recent reports, united’s women’s team are having a tough run in the London and SE League Division 1. Wood said it was a transistional campaign and hard work was going into building the women’s set-up.

Recent findings suggest that there is also work going on behind the scenes to progress the vital redevelopment of the ground, with a fresh pitch and main stand among plans on the table. And Wood thanked fans for continuing to support the club in great numbers.

Industry News: 'A significant shift was necessary' - Crawley Town owners break silence with open letter to fans

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1482 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Reds supporters have been calling out for communication from Raphael Khalili and co following the poor start to the season, the sacking of Colin Kazim-Richards and the embarrassing FA Cup exit to Wimborne Town.
  • But following the club confirming Kevin Blackwell’s appointment as head coach until the end of the season, the ownership group published an open letter to fans.
  • Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Reds supporters have been calling out for communication from Raphael Khalili and co following the poor start to the season, the sacking of Colin Kazim-Richards and the embarrassing FA Cup exit to Wimborne Town.

But following the club confirming Kevin Blackwell’s appointment as head coach until the end of the season, the ownership group published an open letter to fans.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

In the letter they ‘take full responsibility for the direction of this football club’ and recognised ‘significant shift in direction was necessary’ and that ‘difficult decisions have now been made’.

They also gave updates on strengthening the club’s leadership and the the ownership group.

Here is the open letter in full:.

From the Ownership Group and Board of Directors of Crawley Town Football Club.

First and foremost, we want to thank every Crawley Town supporter for their continued patience, loyalty and commitment to this Football Club during what has undoubtedly been a difficult period.

In a recent development, we recognise that our start to the season has fallen well below the standards we expect, and more importantly, the standards that you, our supporters, deserve. We understand the frustration, the disappointment and the questions being asked. We also recognise that our communication in recent weeks has not been what it should be.

Over the past month, we have been working tirelessly behind the scenes to assess every aspect of the club and put in place the new structures and processes required to take us forward into a positive new chapter.

As owners, we take full responsibility for the direction of this football club. We have never underestimated the privilege of being entrusted with Crawley Town, nor the responsibilities and expectations that come with it.

Industry observers note that it became clear that a significant shift in direction was necessary. Some difficult decisions have now been made, but we firmly believe they are the best decisions for protecting the long-term interests of Crawley Town Football Club.

Today, we want to share with you some of the changes that we are making in order to demonstrate our commitment to changing the direction of the Club for the better.

First Team Management: Following the recent changes to our football management structure, we undertook an extensive search to identify the right person to lead Crawley Town going forward.

Over the past several weeks, we have spoken with and interviewed numerous experienced and highly regarded managers. Throughout this process, our priority has always been to make the right appointment for the Club, rather than rushing into a decision.

Recent findings suggest that at the same time, we have been extremely encouraged by the impact Kevin Blackwell has made since taking charge. His experience, leadership and understanding of the challenges we face have been evident, and we have seen a marked improvement in the players' performances, engagement and attitude.

With the team remaining unbeaten in the league under Kevin's leadership, there have already been encouraging signs of greater stability, resilience and togetherness within the squad.

Having carefully considered all of our options and building upon the positive impact that we have already seen from Kevin, we firmly believe that he is the right man to lead Crawley Town for the remainder of the season, and we are pleased to confirm his appointment as First Team Manager.

Kevin has our full confidence and support, and we will be further strengthening his coaching team with the addition of another assistant coach in due course.

Our immediate focus is now on giving Kevin, his staff and the players every opportunity to succeed, restoring confidence and building the consistency required to climb the league table.

Strengthening the Club's Leadership: We are currently in the process of strengthening our senior executive structure to provide greater expertise and support across both our football and off-field operations.

We expect to provide further details subject to the necessary approvals from the Independent Football Regulator (IFR) and the EFL.

We believe that establishing a strong, experienced and accountable executive structure is fundamental to building a successful and sustainable football club.

Strengthening Our Ownership Group: We are delighted to announce and welcome Jonathan Meller to our Ownership Group. Jonathan brings extensive experience and knowledge from more than a decade of involvement in football and has a long-standing relationship with members of our Ownership Group. He has experience in helping clubs progress and sees Crawley Town as the perfect opportunity to help a club grow and move up the leagues.

We believe Jonathan's insight, relationships and understanding of the industry will be another valuable addition as we continue to develop the Club.

In a recent development, recruitment, Data and Football Operations: Our review has also identified the need to modernise and strengthen the way the Club operates, particularly in the areas of player recruitment, performance analysis and internal processes. We will be able to announce the appointment of a fresh Head of Recruitment in the days/coming weeks, who will play an important role in contributing to our future football strategy. In parallel, we are developing a comprehensive new data-led and eyes-on recruitment strategy, alongside improved systems and processes throughout the Club.

Our ambition is to build a more intelligent, efficient and structured football operation, where recruitment decisions are supported by robust analysis, clear football principles and a long-term vision and culture.

These changes will not happen overnight, but they are essential if we are to establish the foundations for lasting success.

Industry observers note that commercial Growth and Fresh Opportunities: Off the pitch, we are equally focused on developing the Club's commercial potential and creating opportunities that extend beyond the traditional boundaries of a League Two football club. We are in the final stages of an exciting new commercial partnership, which we expect to announce shortly.

We believe this relationship has the potential to introduce Crawley Town to a significantly wider, global audience, creating newly introduced opportunities for the Club, our partners and our supporters.

Our ambition remains to build a club that is competitive on the pitch, commercially progressive off it and firmly connected to its community.

We appreciate that announcements, words and promises ultimately mean very little without results on the pitch.

It has been revealed that we will be judged by our actions, and rightly so: We are not asking anyone to ignore the difficulties of recent months or pretend that everything has been good enough. It hasn't. But we do ask that we now look forward together rather than backwards and divided.

According to recent reports, football is never a straight line. Every club experiences difficult periods, setbacks and moments when its character is tested. It is during these moments, more than any other, that the strength of a football club's community becomes so key.

It has been revealed that the supporters are, and always will be, the heartbeat of Crawley Town. Your loyalty, your passion and your support are what give this Club its identity and purpose.

We understand that support must be earned through performances and results, and we accept our responsibility to deliver both. However, we also believe that the strongest football clubs are those that stand together through the difficult moments, not just the successful ones.

And that brings us to Fleetwood.

It has been revealed that our upcoming fixture against Fleetwood is an crucial moment for this football club. We want to use it as an opportunity to draw a line under the difficult start to our season and begin a fresh chapter, together. Fill the stands, make your voices heard and get behind Kevin and the players from the very first whistle.

We know the difference a united crowd can make, particularly when a team needs confidence and belief.

It has been revealed that let Fleetwood be the moment we come together, turn the page and start building the momentum that will define the rest of our season: There is still a long way to go, plenty of football to be played and everything to fight for. We have absolute belief in our ability to turn our fortunes around.

Industry observers note that we remain as committed and determined today as we were on the day we took ownership of this Football Club. Our ambition has not changed, and neither has our belief in what Crawley Town can become. There will undoubtedly be further challenges along the way, but we are determined to face them with honesty, resilience and a shared sense of purpose.

Industry observers note that to every supporter who has continued to turn up, travel, sing and stand by the team during this difficult period, thank you. Your commitment does not go unnoticed or unappreciated.

For and on behalf of the Ownership Group & Board of Directors Crawley Town Football Club​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Sam Varley | 19 Nov 2026 23:09.
  • Bradford City and Doncaster Rovers will square off on Saturday in a Yorkshire derby with importance at both ends of the League One table.
  • The hosts sit a point outside of the playoff places following a defeat last time out while their visitors have dropped into the bottom four due to consecutive losses.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Sam Varley | 19 Nov 2026 23:09.

Bradford City and Doncaster Rovers will square off on Saturday in a Yorkshire derby with importance at both ends of the League One table.

The hosts sit a point outside of the playoff places following a defeat last time out while their visitors have dropped into the bottom four due to consecutive losses.

Bradford City head into their first League One game of November at the weekend following an international break with the hopes of returning to winning ways and moving back into the top six.

After winning promotion from League Two and losing in the League One playoffs in the last two seasons, the Bantams picked up where they left off in early 2026-27, winning five of their first seven outings before Graham Alexander departed for Preston North End.

They then turned to Michael Duff and have struggled to continue their hot start since, winning one, drawing four and losing one of their last six league matches with the only victory coming against Stevenage in mid-October.

That did form part of a run of four straight clean sheets for the Bantams, who top the division with nine and have conceded a league-low tally of eight goals, but that came to an end in their last league outing against fellow promotion-chasers and Yorkshire rivals Huddersfield Town, who dished out a 3-0 beating at Mbanq Valley Parade.

Now, at least, on the back of a pair of confidence-boosting cup wins before their break, beating Marine 7-0 in the FA Cup and York City 4-0 in the EFL Trophy, Bradford City now sit eighth, but just two points off fourth spot, and will hope to retake a top-six spot and kickstart another hot streak in League One.

Their visitors, meanwhile, make the trip across Yorkshire in search of a return to winning ways of their own in their battle at the other end of League One.

Doncaster Rovers also won promotion from League Two in 2024-25 and finished 14th last time around on their return to the second tier but now find themselves 21st with just 12 points on the board from 13 games.

That is in no small part down to a poor away record, having lost five of seven games on the road, collected just four points and conceded 16 goals in those.

Two heavy away defeats have come consecutively for Grant McCann's side since a home victory over Sheffield Wednesday, as they lost 3-1 at Luton Town and 6-1 in their last third-tier match away at MK Dons at the end of October.

Having also since played two cup games, beating Rochdale in the EFL Trophy and losing 3-0 away at non-league Kidderminster Harriers in the FA Cup, Doncaster Rovers now head into a tough trip aiming to kickstart an upturn in form in League One and climb out of the bottom four.

Bradford City form (all competitions):.

Doncaster Rovers League One form:.

Doncaster Rovers form (all competitions):.

Bradford City remain without wide men Josh Neufville and Tyreik Wright, while attacker Bobby Pointon also missed their last outing through injury.

Corey O'Keeffe will continue in a wing-back role in Neufville's absence, while Antoni Sarcevic will start in midfield having served a suspension in the FA Cup for a red card received in their last league game.

George Lapslie, Adam Phillips and Nick Powell will all compete for starts in attack after Jake Beesley led the line with support from Kayden Jackson and Will Swan in the 3-0 defeat to Huddersfield.

Doncaster Rovers continue to contend with several injury challenges, as James Collins, Francis Okoronkwo, Matty Pearson, James Husband and Tommy O'Reilly should all remain sidelined.

McCann made some rotations in their two cup games and should make changes from the team that lost 6-1 to MK Dons in their last league outing, with the likes of Robbie Gotts and Will Keane pushing to start after being reduced to substitute appearances.

Hakeeb Adelakun will also challenge for a start on the wing and may join Isaac Hutchinson and Jordan Thomas in support of a lone striker unless captain and key man Owen Bailey returns to an advanced midfield role.

Bradford City possible starting lineup:.

McCracken; Pennington, Baldwin, Pratt; O'Keeffe, Sarcevic, Connolly, Touray; Swan, Beesley, Phillips.

Doncaster Rovers possible starting lineup:.

Simkin; Sterry, Grehan, Byrne, Senior; Broadbent, Gotts; Thomas, Bailey, Adelakun; Keane.

Bradford City have certainly not been at their best in League One since Michael Duff's arrival, but still boasting the league's standout defensive record, and having rebuilt confidence with a pair of dominant cup wins, we back them to come out on top at home to a struggling Doncaster team.

AC Milan welcomed back a rejuvenated Goncalo Ramos after the last international break, but they will not do so this time.

In a recent development, as La Gazzetta dello Sport write, Ramos is finding himself ‘trapped in a nightmare season’, which is now also taking its toll on him for the national team too. As a reminder, he scored three goals in three starts (against Norway, Denmark and Norway again) during the September-October break.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

This allowed him to put his struggles behind him for a couple of weeks, but things are now getting tough with the Seleção as well. Last Saturday – in a 4-1 defeat against Denmark – he finished the match without even touching the ball in the penalty box.

It was frighteningly similar to the isolation seen at Milan, and the problem is that his numbers didn’t improve even in Wales. Portugal won 3-2 but not only did the former PSG man not get his name on the scoresheet, he also didn’t participate in any of the goals directly.

Sources indicate that his numbers in the 59 minutes he was on the pitch: 1 shot attempted (a header from Neto’s pass from the left in the 47th minute), 4/7 successful passes, 11 touches, and 1 unsuccessful dribble. The story of a striker who is not involved.

That’s not all, either. Gonçalo also angered Bruno Fernandes. It happened during a counter-attack, with the Portuguese captain breaking down the left and crossing low, expecting Ramos to be there. Gonçalo had stopped though, and Fernandes’s reprimand was inevitable.

The two would later have another exchange at the end of the match, with Bruno reminding his team-mate – who was disappointed to be brought off after less than an hour – of the responsibility of replacing a giant like Cristian Ronaldo. Oh, and Bruno Fernandes has been linked today, by the way.

In short, Goncalo Ramos is ‘twisted in a spiral he can’t seem to escape’. After the game in Cardiff last night, he has reached 661 minutes without a goal for club and country. The last one was exactly a month ago, on October 18th against Atalanta.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Reds, who have confirmed Kevin Blackwell as boss until the end of the season, are right now bottom of League Two, six points adrift of safety but with three games in hand.

Every game is crucial from now on but the owners, in an open letter to fans, see Saturday’s game at the Broadfield Stadium as ‘an important moment’ for the club.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

They want to draw a line under what has happened so far this season and move on, starting with three points and their first home win of the season.

It has been revealed that in the open letter, they stated: “Our upcoming fixture against Fleetwood is an crucial moment for this football club. We want to use it as an opportunity to draw a line under the difficult start to our season and begin a fresh chapter, together. Fill the stands, make your voices heard and get behind Kevin and the players from the very first whistle.

“We know the difference a united crowd can make, particularly when a team needs confidence and belief.”.

Blackwell’s side still have 34 games left this season, so there is still plenty of time to turn things around, and they believe that can happen for the Reds.

They added: “Let Fleetwood be the moment we come together, turn the page and start building the momentum that will define the rest of our season: There is still a long way to go, plenty of football to be played and everything to fight for. We have absolute belief in our ability to turn our fortunes around.

According to recent reports, “We remain as committed and determined today as we were on the day we took ownership of this Football Club. Our ambition has not changed, and neither has our belief in what Crawley Town can become. There will undoubtedly be further challenges along the way, but we are determined to face them with honesty, resilience and a shared sense of purpose.

“To every supporter who has continued to turn up, travel, sing and stand by the team during this difficult period, thank you. Your commitment does not go unnoticed or unappreciated.”.

And in his first interview following the news he had been appointed for the remainder of the season, Blackwell told his players to match the fans’ passion and desire.

In a recent development, "It's our club, isn't it? Crawley Town is our club. I've mentioned to the players, you've got to fight every minute that you're out on that pitch. You're not just playing for yourself, you're playing for your family, you're playing for a future, you're playing for the fans. Every one of those fans would love to get off that terrace and be on that green base and play.

“You've got to match that desire that the fans have got. If you do that, the fans will back you, even if you don't win the games. But if you're not seen to be giving everything you've got, I'll let them know, never mind the fans.”.

Michael Carrick had urged his Manchester United players to come out and fight. But nobody could have imagined quite how Lisandro Martínez would interpret that message.

By the end of an extraordinary evening in Madrid, where United went 1-0 down inside a minute and never recovered against Atlético Madrid, Martínez had blown the lid off any pretence of all being well at the club as he introduced a lacerating assault on the club’s executives.

United had come into this getting battered from all sides and when Pablo Barrios put Atlético ahead, Jamie Carragher’s pre-match assessment about how things could get “very messy, very quickly” for all involved at Old Trafford must have been ringing in the ears of the travelling supporters.

It has been revealed that they certainly know how to make life difficult for themselves. Leny Yoro’s 74th-minute red card pretty much ended hopes of them taking something from the game.

Ademola Lookman scored Atlético’s second soon after and Carrick was staring at another defeat. And so they now move on to a big game at Leeds on Sunday. This was not the result Carrick would have wanted – and that is before what happened off the pitch.

Ademola Lookman PUNISHES a 10-man Man United 💥 https://t.co/GHKYIHGhNC.

Another defeat intensified the pressure on Carrick but Martínez left nobody under any illusions that he felt the finger should be pointed not simply at another manager or the players, but the hierarchy above him.

It was extraordinary to see a player speaking out so publicly in this fashion against his own bosses.

But Martínez pulled no punches, even going as far as singling out Jason Wilcox, the director of football, as he criticised the club’s summer transfer business and effectively accused the club of failing Carrick and the players in the window.

To what extent Martínez’s comments mirror the views of the wider dressing room is unclear, but you have to wonder where Carrick and United go from here.

Sources indicate that on the one hand, Martínez was providing a show of support for his manager by attacking the people above him. At the same time, he has presented Carrick with a disciplinary problem to address.

Lisandro Martínez did NOT hold back after United's loss to Atletico 😬👀 https://t.co/OGo25Pzd30.

And United have enough troubles as it is without a senior member of Carrick’s dressing room turning so squarely against the club’s power brokers.

Industry observers note that martínez was probably only giving voice to what many fans have been saying since an underwhelming transfer window closed with more questions than answers. But for a player to talk in such blunt, excoriating terms resonated more loudly than anything a supporter or United’s most caustic critic could say.

The message was simple: you can sack all the managers you want but until you pull together a squad worthy of United’s name and give the man at the helm the tools to compete, the club will struggle to escape this cycle of mediocrity.

Industry observers note that no one can reasonably argue United’s window was a success. They went into it with the hopes of landing Elliot Anderson and other premium midfielders but ended up going for numbers over proven quality or pedigree. Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba were not a trio of signings anyone expected at the start of summer, not even the club itself.

There were glaring problems to address in defence, not least at left-back, and at centre-forward but a quality alternative to Luke Shaw never materialised and no back-up was signed for Benjamin Sesko, who was missing for four months with a shin injury that has since resurfaced and which could keep him out for a while yet.

Having done so well to lead United to third and take them back into the Champions League, Carrick would have expected further backing than he got in the summer. Ever the tech giant man, he has been too polite to criticise that lack of investment. But the cat is out of the bag now Martínez has had his say.

It now places the spotlight on Wilcox. United head to Elland Road on Sunday and that was the scene of Rúben Amorim’s final meltdown as manager. Two days after he blew up in a meeting with Wilcox at United’s Carrington training base, Amorim took aim at the director of football and others at the club, demanding they “do their job” and repeatedly declaring that he had come to Old Trafford to “be the manager, not to be the coach”.

It is remarkable to think that, 10 months on, United head back to Leeds with just as many questions as there were back then.

United’s worst start to a league season for 40 years has ensured Carrick is already under pressure, but Martínez is very much of the view that it is no longer enough for the manager and the players to keep carrying the can and that the credibility and suitability of those who recruit the players and make the decisions must now be called into question.

That Martínez picked this game to speak out was interesting. United, lost, yes, and the manner of Atlético’s opening goal from Barrios after 53 seconds was shocking. But United at least went down fighting on this occasion and had fashioned enough good chances to at least draw level before Yoro’s harsh 74th-minute red card swung a delicately poised match decisively in Atlético’s favour.

Lookman made it 2-0 soon after, but Atlético, having looked like they would run all over United in those opening 10 minutes, were made to work hard for their victory.

United cannot keep shooting themselves in the foot like they did in the first minute. Carrick had gone with a three-man midfield to shore things up and made his team more comfortable and yet they were opened up in double quick time by two passes through the middle.

Still, you only needed to look across at United’s opponents to appreciate how chaotic it had become at Old Trafford.

Diego Simeone’s reign at Atlético covers a period stretching two years longer than the post-Ferguson era and in many ways his teams have represented everything United have not been in that time: well constructed and thought through, unified, stable, organised, hungry, aggressive, uncompromising and with a flash of devilment.

If United were not in crisis before this, they are now.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Champions League tie between Atlético Madrid and Manchester United from the Metropolitano. The two sides had contrasting fortunes in their opening fixtures in this competition, Man Utd beating Azerbaijan’s Sabah 4-0 at Old Trafford a month ago while Atléti were defeated by Liverpool who came back from 1-0 down to win 2-1.

According to recent reports, but domestically it is the other way round – Michael Carrick’s side have made the club’s worst start in the league for 40 years with one win, three draws and two defeats and have been knocked out of the League Cup. Those of us who watch them regularly – purely because of occupational obligations in this instance – have been surprised by how poor they have been. The results have been bad but the performances even worse.

They seem to lack players who can play on the front foot, who have the athletic dynamism required in this league and too many self-indulgent forward players who either can’t be bothered to help out their team-mates or cannot concentrate long enough to do so. Spooked by their lack of pace in defence and midfield, they are hidebound by caution, dropping ever deeper, ever more reliant on counter-attacking despite the blatant disconnect between the front four and back six. If they drift through this match and Sunday’s trip to Elland Road, Carrick may join the long list of Ineos-driven managerial mis-steps.

According to recent reports, atlético have won six of eight in La Liga and have been defeated only once. They are five points behind Barcelona in second and have score 18 goals and let in eight, which may seem a curious thing to include in a preview but it is done to emphasise that many fans’ perception of Diego Simeone’s team are out of date. Back in the days of Diego Godín, Gabi, Juanfran et all, six wins a draw and a defeat would have had goals for of about 10 and goals against of maybe three.

Simeone is a martinet about attitude not systems or styles and his team have evolved, with the World Cup-winner Alex Baena, who has scored four goals so far, driving them on. He has reintegrated Julián Alvarez, too, after his brazen attempt to force a move to Barcelona so incensed Atléti fans that it seemed they would drive him out of the club. Simeone refused to let Alvarez get his own way and he is now buckling down. Ten years ago Simeone would have bitten his head off.

It has been revealed that the one surviving veteran in the squad from that first of El Cholo’s Liga winning sides and the two Champions League finals, victory in which would represent Simeone’s crowning achievement, is the midfielder Koke. And it was after the embarrassing FA Cup exit to seventh tier Wimborne Town that Blackwell gave a scathing verdict on the club’s recruitment over the past 12 months and said somewthing has to change.

Industry observers note that speaking before the Fleetwood game, Blackwell said: “That was the discussions that we've had over the last week, quite heavily about the recruitment and what we need to do. We know where we are. We're identifying and trying to identify players.

“It won't be easy to get them in at this time of the year. It's not the best time of year to be making recruitment, but the owners know that we have to do that and they've been 100 per cent behind it. They've been very inventive in some of their ideas and I've been very impressed.”.

Recent findings suggest that since Blackwell has been in charge, the club have brought in three fresh, experienced players – Connor Wickham, Ben Heneghan and Ayman Benarous – and now the new boss has a huge squad to work with. “When I was taking all of them, all 28 on my own, that was tough,” he remarked.

Recent findings suggest that "That's why I was so pleased with the attitude of the players. Now that we've got Jordan [Tait] in, which is another step forward, another club coach that we've got in here, I'm looking forward to working with the club, working with the players and doing what we've got to do.”.

According to recent reports, and are the likes of Wickham and Heneghan fit too start? “Well, we've had to gradually get Conor and Ben a bit fitter and that's why maybe the international break has helped us a little bit.

"But both of them have got great attitude and have been senior professionals.

“Ben has come in and he quite surprised me with his fitness levels, so we've been able to use these two weeks to try and get them up to speed a little bit better. But they've brought know-how, experience and a voice and those three things are going to be massive for us.”.

Reds face Fleetwood on Saturday before hosting Barnet on Tuesday night.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Nsidibe Akpan | 19 Nov 2026 23:13.
  • Feyenoord host SBV Excelsior at Stadion Feijenoord (De Kuip) in Rotterdam in round 13 of the 2026-27 Eredivisie on Saturday.
  • The Pride of South sit second in the Eredivisie table on 25 points, one behind PSV after losing 5-3 at Heerenveen on November 8, while Excelsior are 15th on 11 points, one clear of the relegation play-off place after five straight league defeats.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Nsidibe Akpan | 19 Nov 2026 23:13.

Feyenoord host SBV Excelsior at Stadion Feijenoord (De Kuip) in Rotterdam in round 13 of the 2026-27 Eredivisie on Saturday.

The Pride of South sit second in the Eredivisie table on 25 points, one behind PSV after losing 5-3 at Heerenveen on November 8, while Excelsior are 15th on 11 points, one clear of the relegation play-off place after five straight league defeats.

Giovanni van Bronckhorst's side arrive without a win in five matches in all competitions, having lost 1-0 at Real Betis on October 21, drawn 1-1 with PSV and Fortuna Sittard, lost 3-0 at home to Inter Milan on November 3 and lost 5-3 at Heerenveen.

Heerenveen was Feyenoord's first league defeat of the season, and it came after they led 2-0 through Anis Hadj Moussa and a Nacho Ferri penalty, only for substitute Ringo Meerveld to score a hat-trick.

Their attack has not been the problem, as 36 league goals in 12 games trail only PSV's 40, and a 5-0 home win over Utrecht on September 20 featured two goals from Hadj Moussa plus strikes from Ferri, Luciano Valente and Gaoussou Diarra.

The damage is coming at the other end, where Feyenoord have conceded seven goals in their last three league games after allowing 10 in the first nine, and they have let in at least one in each of their last five matches in all competitions.

Goalkeeper Tjark Ernst, signed from Hertha BSC for €5m in the summer, received sarcastic applause from home supporters after a routine catch against Inter, and Opta figures published by NOS rate only two Eredivisie goalkeepers worse than him at keeping out shots, although Van Bronckhorst continues to select him.

Captain Valente remarked after the Heerenveen defeat that things clearly had to change, while Van Bronckhorst has said that opponents have adapted to the way Feyenoord play.

Ruben den Uil's side won 4-0 at Cambuur in their opening game to go top of the Eredivisie for the first time in 47 years, and they had 10 points from five games after a draw at NEC on September 8.

Since then Excelsior have taken one point from a possible 21, a run of seven games that includes a 2-2 draw at Ajax on September 19 despite being outshot 33-8, a 1-5 home loss to Groningen and a 4-0 defeat at Heerenveen on October 16.

In their last five league games, Excelsior have conceded 20 goals and scored once, a stretch that includes a 9-0 defeat by Twente on November 1, the heaviest in the club's league history, in which Nesto Groen was sent off after five minutes for a challenge on Robin Propper.

Go Ahead Eagles then won 1-0 at Excelsior on November 7 through Soren Tengstedt, in a game Den Uil described as a typical 0-0, which left the Kralingers without a goal in four league games and on 16 for the season, four of which came in the opening win at Cambuur.

Aymen Sliti, who has three league goals, and defender Jan Plug are both on loan from Feyenoord, and Sliti has mentioned he will not celebrate if he scores at De Kuip.

Feyenoord have eased the restrictions on visiting supporters for the derby, who will not be required to use organised transport to De Kuip.

Feyenoord form (all competitions):.

SBV Excelsior form (all competitions):.

Hadj Moussa is a major doubt after a sprained ankle on international duty with Algeria following the game against Togo, and Feyenoord-watcher Martijn Krabbendam stated on Voetbal International's podcast that reaching the derby will be difficult, with the club aiming to have him ready for the Klassieker against Ajax on November 29, although Kicker reported that he left the Algeria camp after a dispute with the coach rather than through injury.

Jeremiah St. Juste is still out with a shin problem and Van Bronckhorst hopes to have him back before the winter break, while Bart Nieuwkoop, Jordan Bos and Thomas Beelen are not expected until after it and Tijme Wessels is recovering from knee surgery.

Reiss Nelson and Shaqueel van Persie are available again after injuries, Gijs Smal has returned to group training and Jakub Moder, who has played one minute this season, is also being eased back, although neither is certain for Saturday and no Feyenoord player is suspended.

For the visitors, Groen misses the derby serving the last game of a three-match ban, with one match suspended, for the red card against Twente, which leaves Mario Dominguez or David Garden to lead the line.

Sliti hurt his hand in the Netherlands Under-21s' 3-2 defeat by Denmark on November 17 and fears a bruised or broken thumb, but he has remarked he expects to play on Saturday, with former Feyenoord winger Alireza Jahanbakhsh the alternative on the flank.

Feyenoord possible starting lineup:.

Ernst; Read, Watanabe, Marmol, Lopez; Zechiel, Vanhoutte, Targhalline; Van Persie, Ferri, Valente.

SBV Excelsior possible starting lineup:.

Van Gassel; Bos, Plug, Widell, Meissen; Yegoian, Hartjes; Naujoks, Thorsteinsson, Sliti; Dominguez.

Feyenoord have won each of their last six meetings with Excelsior, scoring at least twice every time, including 2-1 wins on August 16, 2025 and March 15, 2026, and Excelsior have not won at De Kuip since 1980.

That record matters because this Excelsior side has conceded 20 goals in five league games, has lost Groen up front and faces an attack that has scored 36 times in 12 league games.

Feyenoord's own defence, which has conceded in five straight matches, and the possible absence of Hadj Moussa leave a small opening, but Excelsior have failed to score in each of their last four league games, so we expect Van Bronckhorst's side to win without needing to rely on one player.

The 67-year-old was confirmed as boss for the remainder of the 2026/27 campaign on Thursday (November 19) after a month as interim head coach following the sacking of Colin Kazim-Richards in October.

Reds are currently bottom of League Two and out of every cup competition and the the former Leeds United boss knows it will be a tough job getting his side up the table – but he believes they can do it.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

"Obviously we're disappointed with the cup results, there's no doubt about that, but the league form is what I've come to do and try and sort out,” he stated.

“If the players just give me what they've given me in training, then I know we'll be okay.

"We've got a long hard fight on our hands and that's why everybody's pulling together. As I remarked, the ownership where the club needs to be going and they've expressed that they want to bring newly introduced staff in, which we've already started and we're going to hopefully bring someone else in.

In a recent development, “We're looking at new recruitment, the whole lot, getting the club back on its feet again. So, yes, it's an exciting time, but a tough time.”.

The first thing on Blackwell's mind will be how to get his side to stat winning in the league and he laid out how they start to do that. He said: “I think the first thing you do is, if you're in a hole, stop digging. I think clearly, now as the club's stopped digging, we've now got to get out of the hole. But if that support is there, and we know it is, and the dynamics of the owners, they know what they want for the club.

As I said, if you look around the place, this club is in decent shape, but we've now got to match the ambition of the owners on the pitch. That's my job now and the players'. We've got to support the owner with what they've done for us and say thank you.

“The only way we can do that is in the league.”.

According to recent reports, blackwell noted he would not have believed he would be appointed long-term when he was first around the club but highlighted the players have had a massive say on what has happened. “The thing that's impressed me now is the attitude of the players. I've enjoyed coming in training and that's half a job, is if you enjoy doing your job,” he said.

“I love football, but there's been times even in my career where you think, I've got to go in today and face the players and whatever. They've been a joy to come in and they've worked really hard. Some of them have struggled, but they've still given it a go and that's the sort of attitude I'm looking for.

Recent findings suggest that “We must have that never-say-die attitude, because if we don't have that, then we are in trouble. But so far, the players have really responded and I'm really pleased and that's really one of the big factors as to why I've decided to stay.”.

In the coming weeks, Kevin will be making further appointments to his coaching team, following the recent arrival of Jordan Tait.

A statement from ownership will follow shortly.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Derek McInnes has stressed that Rangers have no intention of selling their key players in January as he looks to maintain the club’s growing momentum ahead of Saturday night’s Premiership clash with Motherwell.

The Ibrox boss believes retaining the core of his squad will be vital to Rangers’ silverware ambitions this season, insisting that the club has no desire to part with regular starters despite potential interest from elsewhere.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

While conceding that an offer too good to turn down would have to be considered, McInnes emphasised that Rangers are keen to avoid disruption to the squad when the winter transfer window opens.

Industry observers note that “We will be keeping them,” he declared emphatically. “We're not looking to move players out, certainly players who have been playing regularly. We want to shut that down really early. We know and understand that keeping that core of players and having that stability is so crucial for us.”.

Rangers return to league action against a Motherwell side McInnes claims is beginning to rediscover the qualities that made them such a formidable opponent last season under Jens Berthel Askou.

They head to Fir Park aiming to extend their 12-game unbeaten run, but McInnes anticipates a difficult test against a Motherwell side that has shown signs of improvement under Alfred Johansson’s care in recent weeks.

Recent findings suggest that “I think they've started to look a wee bit more like that team that got a lot of success last year,” McInnes admitted. “They've got a lot of traits and similarities. They've lost two or three key players, but they still have the nucleus of that team and you can see they've got a clear idea of what they're trying to do.

Recent findings suggest that “The difficulty when you go away from home is obvious. You've got to make sure you do so much right. It's not just about being good technically. You've got to make sure that all the other facets are there, that you need to compete right from the outset.”.

McInnes highlighted Rangers’ recent away win at St Mirren as a blueprint for Saturday’s encounter, adding: “Something similar will be required. If we want to get to where we want to get to this season, it's a game that presents us with three points. And we want to make sure we leave Motherwell with all three, if we can.”.

Rangers have kept eight clean sheets during their near two-month unbeaten run, with McInnes eager for his side to maintain their defensive solidity as they enter a demanding run of fixtures.

“I don't like it when we're too comfortable," he explained. “If we're four or five up and we’re deep into the second half, then I'll be all fine. But when the game is still in the balance, particularly away from home, and you're 1-0 up or 2-0 up, there's still work to do.

In a recent development, “We should be proud of that [clean sheets], but I thought we put it at risk a wee bit once or twice against St Mirren and I think it was unnecessary. We've got to make sure that we don't get complacent with what we're doing and we stay on top of the job.".

In a recent development, with three consecutive home fixtures following Saturday's trip to North Lanarkshire, Rangers have an opportunity to build further momentum. McInnes, however, knows the immediate priority is on overcoming a rejuvenated Motherwell side.

“We're not expecting it to be straightforward,” he stated. “But I do expect us to bring a strong performance if we're going to win the game. I think everybody, certainly me and the staff, and I'm sure the supporters are the same, are starting to see a team that we think we can get behind and get a bit of confidence from.”.

There was positive news on the injury front following the international break, with Daisuke Yokota returning to training earlier this week alongside Ross McCrorie, while Lawrence Shankland and Cammy Devlin are continuing their rehabilitation through increased work on the grass.

Mato, 23, played just three league games for Hearts after arriving on an initial loan from North Macedonian outfit FK Vardar last January, but has featured regularly for the Gorgie side this season after making his move permanent in the summer by penning a three-year contract in July.

Industry observers note that originally signed as a wide forward, the Ugandan international was deployed as a left-back against Turkish outfit Trabzonspor in the Europa League earlier this month, with Hearts’ injury crisis seeing Mato pitted against former Liverpool icon, Mo Salah. However, he admits it’s another ex-Anfield hero, Senegal international Sadio Mane, that he takes inspiration from as he looks ahead to the African Cup of Nations in his homeland next summer.

Sources indicate that “I grew up just watching the other players on TV and sneaking in the stadiums,” Mato told RG. “I didn't even have a chance to be like a ball boy to give them the balls in the national team. I only did that on the club level. But wearing the national team jersey is a significant responsibility, we're representing our families, our dream, and millions of Ugandans.

“Mane is my all-time favourite African player. I would love to wear the captain's armband. I would love to lead my country. We grow by responsibilities, not by age. So, that would have a massive impact and would be a massive confidence booster for me to be leading the nation to glory.”.

Sources indicate that the 23-year-old indicates he is using the pain of defeat to fuel another of his major dreams - bringing silverware at Tynecastle. Refusing to concede his side are out of the title race this season despite being 11 points behind league leaders Celtic, he admits the crushing way that a first top flight title win since 1960 trophy was ripped from their grasp by two late Hoops goal on the final day last season still stings.

“It's been ups and downs [since joining Hearts],” he admits. “Coming from Macedonia, playing 90-plus minutes and then coming on for Hearts and playing for 13 minutes in three games and 13 minutes in the second half of the season. It's been ups and downs, but with patience, everything will come to an end.

“I just had to come here and wait for my time, but every time we just have to be patient. I needed to work hard on myself, work hard for the team, so I can get more game time. It's all about mentality. You have to adapt to any coach that comes your way. If you don't adapt, you're dead as a footballer. Last season was hectic and brutal for the team, for the fans. Those last minutes [vs Celtic], it was a heartbreak for everyone, for every Hearts fan. It was a total disaster.

Industry observers note that “But we're looking forward to give it all this season. But suddenly we got a lot of injuries here and there, but those who are still fit, we're trying our best to still keep [the title race] alive for our friends, our brothers who are injured, so they can come and join us [when they're back]. Because we can't let it down, we still have to keep the hopes for the first place.".

It's a record he can add to his already-extensive collection, which includes being the youngest Champions League player, the youngest Premier League goalscorer, and the youngest Premier League winner.

Max Dowman became England Under-21s' youngest-ever goal scorer when he scored against France on Monday.

'Obviously all the players in the squad are under pressure from their clubs and the expectation that surrounds them, so as much as we can we have to make that as easy as we can.'.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Nsidibe Akpan | 19 Nov 2026 23:31.
  • FC Groningen host SC Heerenveen in the Eredivisie at Euroborg on Saturday, November 21 in the first Derby of the North of the 2026-27 season.
  • Sixth-placed Heerenveen arrive on 21 points on the Eredivisie table after four consecutive league wins, while ninth-placed Groningen have taken one point from their last four games and will be without their head coach, goalkeeper and first-choice right-back.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Nsidibe Akpan | 19 Nov 2026 23:31.

FC Groningen host SC Heerenveen in the Eredivisie at Euroborg on Saturday, November 21 in the first Derby of the North of the 2026-27 season.

Sixth-placed Heerenveen arrive on 21 points on the Eredivisie table after four consecutive league wins, while ninth-placed Groningen have taken one point from their last four games and will be without their head coach, goalkeeper and first-choice right-back.

Groningen have collected one point from their last four Eredivisie matches, a run that began with a 2-5 home defeat to Ajax on October 18 and included a 2-2 draw at NEC Nijmegen.

Those four games have cost 14 goals, and the 2-3 home loss to Sparta Rotterdam on November 1 came after Jacob Ondrejka scored after 17 seconds, before a miscommunication between Etienne Vaessen and Hans Hateboer handed Andrej Kostic the winner in the 85th minute.

The latest setback came at AZ on November 8, where De Trots van het Noorden led 3-1 after 54 minutes, lost 4-3 to a Mexx Meerdink penalty in the 91st minute and finished with nine men after Vaessen collected a second yellow card for protesting the penalty and Hateboer was sent off in the 10th minute of stoppage time for a deliberate handball.

Euroborg has offered little protection this season, with Groningen winning two, drawing one and losing three of their six home league games, and a 2-0 home defeat to Dick Lukkien’s former club FC Emmen ended their KNVB Cup run in the first round on October 29.

The recent derby record still favours the hosts, who won 2-1 at Euroborg on August 16, 2025 through a stoppage-time Brynjolfur Darri Willumsson goal and 2-0 at Abe Lenstra Stadion on January 18, 2026, when captain Thijmen Blokzijl scored the second.

The off-field story is Lukkien, who had a hip replacement last week and remarked the derby arrived “just too early” for his recovery, so assistant Casper Goedkoop will coach from the touchline.

Heerenveen have won four consecutive league games since a 2-0 defeat at PSV Eindhoven, beating Excelsior 4-0, ADO Den Haag 3-2, NEC Nijmegen 1-0 and Feyenoord 5-3.

Those wins have brought 13 goals and five conceded, including two from Jacob Trenskow at ADO on October 24, and have lifted De Superfriezen to 21 points from 12 games with a goal difference of +8.

The 5-3 win over Feyenoord on November 8 ended the unbeaten league record of the Eredivisie leaders, with Heerenveen recovering from 2-0 down after 31 minutes through Maas Willemsen, Levi Smans and a late Ringo Meerveld hat-trick.

Meerveld came on at half time for Maxence Rivera and scored in the 61st, 84th and 93rd minutes, with Trenskow providing the pass for the first of them.

Away from Abe Lenstra Stadion, Robin Veldman’s side have won two, drawn two and lost one of their five league trips, but they have not won in Groningen since a 2-0 victory on March 19, 2023.

Veldman noted after the Feyenoord game that his players wanted to extend the run, and a win would take them further clear of seventh-placed Fortuna Sittard, who sit on 20 points.

Groningen form (all competitions):.

Heerenveen form (all competitions):.

Vaessen and Hateboer are both suspended after their red cards at AZ, so Lovro Stubljar, who has been on the bench in recent league games, is expected to start in goal and Wouter Prins should move in at right-back.

Malcolm Jeng remains out with an Achilles tendon injury and goalkeeper Rijk Janse is also sidelined, while Travis Hernes and Ryan Metu are doubtful after several weeks out.

Heerenveen have no reported injuries or suspensions, so Veldman has a full squad to choose from.

Meerveld is expected to push Rivera for a start on the left of the attacking three after his hat-trick off the bench.

Groningen possible starting lineup:.

Stubljar; Prins, Blokzijl, Rente, Csinger; De Jonge, Clement; Schreuders, Van Bergen, Ondrejka; Willumsson.

Heerenveen possible starting lineup:.

Klaverboer; Braude, Kersten, Willemsen, Zagaritis; Linday, Courtens; Trenskow, Smans, Meerveld; Vente.

Heerenveen have scored 13 goals in their last four league games and have already shown they can recover from a two-goal deficit, while Groningen have conceded at least two goals in each of their last four and lose both Vaessen and Hateboer from the back line.

Groningen have won the last two derbies and have scored at least twice in each of their last four games, so Heerenveen will concede, and the crowd will matter with Lukkien watching from home.

The gap is in defensive organisation rather than attacking quality, and a Heerenveen side with a full squad and a 13-5 goal record over four wins should edge a high-scoring derby by one goal.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Former Celtic winger Aiden McGeady has revealed that a former Parkhead teammate became so addicted to computer games that he was rated as one of the world’s highest-ranked players.

McGeady’s comments arrive on the back of the highly anticipated launch of Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI), which was released on November 19 and is expected to be the best-selling action-adventure video game of all time, having already shattered launch records.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Generating an estimated $1.65 billion across over 17 million pre-order copies before its release, GTA VI is the first release in the franchise from Rockstar Games, which has a flagship development studio based in Edinburgh, in 13 years, and has several celebrity fans that include footballers Erling Haaland, Declan Rice and Thibaut Courtois.

"Tommy Gravesen would play Call of Duty when I was at Celtic,” said McGeady. “We had a group, so we'd go home from training and play it. Tommy would never give us his gamertag. I don't know why, but I don't think he wanted us playing with him. But apparently he was like third or fourth in the world at Call of Duty on team deathmatch.

"Somebody managed to get his gamertag and added him and he had 45 days of playing time. 45 days of playing time! You look down the list of your friends and the next one after him was like two days and Tommy had 45 days. So we were like, Tommy must have been going home and just sitting there all day and all night. So yeah, I mean it is addictive isn't it? I have seen it in football before, lads staying up until like three or four in the morning before a game to play Call of Duty and stuff like that. Not ideal, but what are you going to do?".

However, despite the popularity of GTA VI, the 40-year-old doesn’t expect any current professionals to follow in the footsteps Celtic, Everton and Real Madrid. McGeady admits he has seen several players take portable games consoles on the team coach when headed to away games, and the ex-Celtic and Hibs man has warned the younger generation to not follow Gravesen’s example.

“I don't think GTA VI would be a problem because anybody that brings a portable PlayStation or a portable Xbox, they're obsessed with it anyway, aren't they?” McGeady mentioned, speaking to BOYLE Sports. I've been on buses before and it's like lads will get the PlayStations out and it's like FIFA or Call of Duty or it's Fortnite, whatever it is. Lads do that anyway, they're obsessed with it anyway.

"So I don't think GTA VI is going to create a upcoming breed of a new market of players who are just going to start playing PlayStation. I think the people that already play it will play it anyway. I think most footballers are fairly responsible and most Premier League footballers are fairly responsible. I don't think it's going to take over their life. Maybe for the younger players it could be an glitch because they can be addicted to these games.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Rooks were held to a goalless draw at The Dripping Pan last Saturday by a stubborn Stanway Rovers side who started the day bottom of the Isthmian Premier Division table.

However, they responded well in midweek by avoiding a Sussex Senior Cup upset at 21st-placed Isthmian South East Division side Eastbourne Town, winning 2-1 at The Saffrons.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

After both games, manager Craig Nelson admitted there were areas for his side to improve.

Following the Stanway game, which was Nelson’s 100th match in charge of the Rooks, the 40-year-old said: “For me, we had too many players [who] it felt like [were] going through the motions.

Industry observers note that “The intensity felt a bit low, and the ball speed was low. We breached their backline so many times, but the quality beyond that, for me, was a little bit too low to come away with a victory.

It has been revealed that “Other than the first chance in the early minutes from Noel [Fisher], where for me he should score, I don't remember us having a clear-cut chance. So, not a great day at the office, in my opinion.”.

Despite being more fluent in attack at Eastbourne Town, with an impressive performance from debutant Kwesi Ntim playing a big part, Lewes still lacked some ruthlessness after going 2-0 up.

Afterwards, Nelson stated: “I think we had moments. They're always going to make the game difficult for us, and the conditions obviously don't help.

“We had some good moments in the second half. Probably more opportunities to score. On another day, you probably leave here with a bit more.

Industry observers note that “I think sometimes in cup games, the performance is secondary to actually progressing. We wanted to make sure that we put a strong outfit out because we want to progress in the cup, and we've done that, so happy days.”.

Lewes can celebrate a first appearance in the Senior Cup’s Quarter-Finals since the 2019-20 season as a result, and will learn their opponents when the draw is expected to take place in the next fortnight.

In the meantime, the Rooks make the 171-mile round trip to Ramsgate FC this Saturday, with the Rams sitting just three points behind Nelson’s side in 6th place.

The Kent side are the third-highest goalscorers in the league so far with 38 goals from 17 games, while Callum Jones’ 10 league strikes make him the division’s second-best individual goalscorer.

Nelson said: “Ramsgate is a really hostile place to go. They're going to be quick and physical, so we have to make sure that we bring that work ethic and match exactly what the game demands of us.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Aberdeen chief executive Adrian Bevington is confident the club are set for a period of stability following the appointment of Mario Frick as manager on a two-and-a-half-year contract.

It has been revealed that the Pittodrie club have had three managers this year alone. Four of the last five appointments failed to reach the 50-match mark. Stephen Robinson, Frick’s predecessor, lasted just 28 games.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

“That (stability) is the objective here," remarked Bevington, who himself only joined Aberdeen less than three months ago. "What I would say is we have gone through a really robust process. It wasn't just looking at one or two names. The wider search to begin with was extensive then we narrowed it down.”.

The former Club England managing director admitted the process of identifying a latest manager began before Robinson was relieved of his duties after the recent 4-0 home defeat to Hibs.

“Any club nowadays, or most clubs, would always have some prep work going on, just as a matter of course,” he remarked. I think it's very difficult for clubs to be able to react to a situation if they've not already had some prep work going on. That's not any criticism of any individual manager.”.

Recent findings suggest that bevington stressed that Frick had not been appointed on the advice of players. Goalkeeper Marius Muller has been reported as claiming he first suggested the former Luzern manager’s name to sporting director Lutz Pfannenstiel. “We had some player conversations,” noted Bevington. “But they weren’t the decision makers.”.

It has been revealed that stuart Duff, the Youth Phase manager, has been promoted to Frick’s first-team coaching staff, while Craig Hinchcliffe remains goalkeeper coach. Bevington stressed it was important for Frick to be supported by those with knowledge of the club’s youth players.

Aberdeen at the moment has 24 players out on loan with various clubs, including striker Alfie Bavidge and full-back Dylan Lobban at Inverness Caledonian Thistle and Dunfermline respectively. There has been a clamour for Bavidge and Lobban to return.

“There's conversations going on at the moment as to what we're going to do moving forward,” said Bevington. I believe that we have capability to recall certainly a number of the players. I'd need to look at every individual contract.”.

We often take pride in Scotland in our more authentic, less corrupted professional football. Sure, it lacks the glitz and glamour of the English game, awash with American and Middle Eastern money, but as a result it has remained more rooted in our communities, and more accessible to the working class fans who made the game great in the first place.

The recent Man City scandal has only served to sharpen this contrast. While Pep Guardiola’s teams played undeniably beautiful football, the subsequent revelations of financial impropriety have put the validity of their titles under question and damaged the sporting credibility of the Premier League.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

It has shone a light on the trade-offs English football has had to make: creating an elite, globally renowned product, but at the cost of affording dubious characters free rein over long-standing, treasured community institutions.

READ MORE: Scotland's most beautiful football ground is such a pastoral delight that even Subbuteo noticed.

Scotland’s approach has been different. There is less money, to be sure, but that has insulated the Scottish game from some of this scandal. As a result, it feels more real, a purer form of the game.

However, the truth is that Scottish football is a tough place to ply your trade. This is especially true in the lower divisions, where I started my career with Cowdenbeath in the early 1980s.

Football at this level couldn’t feel further removed from the clashes between Wall Street billionaires and petrostates so common south of the border. It was hard work and often brutal. Although we might take pride in it, the undeniable truth is that for many clubs further down the pyramid, life is tough. Razor thin margins, poor facilities, and low attendances can make it demanding work both on and off the pitch.

In a recent development, it’s hardly surprising then, contrary to how we might see ourselves, that Scottish clubs are not immune to finding themselves reliant on financial benefactors whose interest in them, and in the areas they represent, is passing. When the money dries up, the very existence of these clubs comes under threat.

It has been revealed that take Gretna FC as an example. In 2008, two years after appearing in the Scottish Cup Final, and enjoying a sustained run in the top-flight for the first time in their history, the club was forced into liquidation. Gretna’s owner, Brooks Mileson, who died later that year, was posthumously declared bankrupt.

Recent findings suggest that this tragic episode indicates the dangers of overreliance on financiers who promise massive and briefly deliver, before things come crashing down; a similar fate very nearly befell Dumbarton FC in 2024, when the club went into administration and were only saved by a takeover at the last minute. When the worst happens, there is little that loyal, matchgoing fans can do other than pick up the pieces and start again.

Responsible stewardship then, in the cutthroat world of the Scottish lower divisions, is worth more than silverware. One standout example of this is my friend, Kevin Mackie, chairman of Brechin City. Since 2021, Kevin has done an incredible job stabilising the fan-owned club after a turbulent few years which saw successive relegations consign them outside the SPFL for the first time in 67 years.

According to recent reports, things are finally looking up; last season, the Hedgemen only narrowly missed out on promotion back into League Two. As I write, they sit third in the Lowland League and are among the favourites to challenge this season.

It has been revealed that this is encouraging progress under Kevin’s astute leadership. It shouldn’t come as a surprise given his extensive experience as a local businessman, running successful car dealerships in the Brechin area for several decades, as well as hotels and commercial properties.

Kevin also understands what Gretna and Dumbarton seemingly didn’t: that reliance on distant financiers is fraught with danger, and that the loyalty that defines the relationship between fan and club is seldom present in the corporate world.

According to recent reports, kevin’s car dealership closed almost overnight when his suppliers; Renault, Nissan, and Dacia, along with their banking subsidiary RCI Bank (now Mobilize Financial Services) terminated supply and financing agreements for unclear reasons. It’s a demonstration that the dangers of financial reliance we see so often in football permeate through many other industries – though there are important differences.

In a recent development, kevin has launched a legal claim in search of answers and closure, but five years on a resolution remains frustratingly elusive. This is what shocks me as a football professional. As a manager, I had to face the press immediately after each game and defend my actions. A string of bad results could easily see me fired.

In business, and in law, this sort of direct accountability can be hard to find. The wheels turn slowly and the process is often very opaque. Troublingly, this culture is now seeping into football, as the lengthy legalistic wrangling over Man City reveals. In Scotland, we may not be immune from this.

Sources indicate that despite these difficulties, Kevin can take inspiration from the Brechin fans who stood by their club throughout some tough years. Dedication and loyal support define football, but business can be a different beast. Although football resembles business more and more each day, with Man City showing the ugliest side of this, we shouldn’t lose sight of what makes the game beautiful, especially north of the border.

According to recent reports, business and the law could learn a lot from what makes football so special, and so popular worldwide. As a dedicated steward of his local team, leading them back from some tough times, Kevin represents that as well as anyone.

Craig Levein is a former Hearts player, Scotland international and manager.

There doesn’t seem much danger of him erupting with joy and bumping his head on the roof of those tight Pittodrie dugouts. Albeit, he will have to wait for the chance to take a bow at the stadium having replaced the sacked Stephen Robinson during the international window. Trips to Rugby Park and then Ibrox await before he can enjoy the comforts of home for the first time against Dundee at the end of this month.

Although there was no game on at Pittodrie on Thursday, Frick's face adorned the jumbo screen in the corner as he was officially welcomed to the club ahead of being “formally unveiled”, as the club described it. Even the empty stadium, he noted, gives him “goosebumps”. He regards it as a temple. Nowhere is the reverential air more intoxicating than in the Sir Alex Ferguson Lounge, where Frick was presented to reporters for the first time. “Pure football,” he said, while gazing at the photographs adorning the walls.

Recent findings suggest that the Aberdeen training facility at Cormack Park is better than anything he encountered in Switzerland, where he played and managed. “It is paradise,” he mentioned. He’s clearly keen to linger awhile, to which the reply might be: Good luck with that. While he occupies a unique position as the first Liechtenstein player to become a professional footballer, Frick is slightly less exceptional when it comes to Aberdeen.

Industry observers note that the 52-year-old is the 27th permanent manager at Pittodrie, stretching back to 1903. That averages out at about one every four-and-a-half years, which isn’t too bad. However, as many as 16 have come and gone since Ferguson left for Old Trafford 40 years ago this month. The recent anniversary celebrations – Manchester United being the ones celebrating rather than Aberdeen, who have rued the day almost ever since – were a reminder of the significance of that November’s morning in 1986, when it was revealed he was heading south.

Recent findings suggest that no club is immune to the difficulties of trying to replace a successful manager, as Manchester United have spent the last 13 years proving. Aberdeen have not been completely feckless without Fergie. A Scottish Cup here, a League Cup there. They haven’t been relegated either. Not yet at least.

Industry observers note that steering the side away from danger is Frick’s first task, starting this weekend against the only team right now below them: Kilmarnock. He knows what’s involved having taken over at his previous club, Luzern, five years ago when they were deep in relegation trouble. They parted tech giant this summer.

Sources indicate that “They were bottom of the table with 18 matches and 11 points when I took over there and the whole environment was similar to now,” he said. “We saved them and progressed from there. Isn’t that what Sebastien Pocognoli trumpeted when he was unveiled as Scotland manager three months ago? The alarm bells might be growing louder for Aberdeen fans. Frick explained his “heavy metal football” philosophy. “It is high pressing, it is counter pressing, it is vertical play and creating many goalscoring chances,” he remarked. “That is heavy metal.”.

Supporters will argue that anything’s better than what a team coached by Frick’s predecessor was producing. As for the vexed question of the captaincy, with Kevin Nisbet giving the impression that the responsibility weighs heavily on him, Frick confirmed the striker will retain the armband against Kilmarnock. “Afterwards, I will have to decide what we do,” he said.

Frick speaks five languages with various levels of proficiency. His German and Italian are perfect. “English I need to improve,” he stated. “I started learning English in school but never used it.” He recently started English tuition online “with an Australian who lives in France” with a view to working at a British club. “My only ambition now is to bring success to Aberdeen,” he said.

Frick relishes the challenge. “I am ready!” he stated. “I have had a five-month holiday! I am full of energy.”.

By Joel Lefevre | 19 Nov 2026 23:33.

Seeking their first-ever away victory in the MLS Cup playoffs, Charlotte FC will visit SeatGeek Stadium on Sunday for game one of their best-of-three series with the Chicago Fire.

The Fire finished fourth in the Eastern Conference this year, losing their last outing 4-3 to the Columbus Crew as they wound up a point above Charlotte, who drew 3-3 with Inter Miami on Decision Day.

Throughout 2026, Chicago were out to prove that last year was no fluke as they continued to improve in the league yet again.

In his second year as head coach, Gregg Berhalter saw his team gain two more points than in his inaugural campaign, while finishing four places higher in the Eastern Conference table this time around and making the playoffs on successive occasions.

The next step will be for the Fire to find some playoff success, with this club aiming to advance beyond the first round for the first time since 2009.

During this regular season campaign, they won three more home matches when compared to 2025, though they have only won one playoff fixture in Illinois since 2009, defeating Orlando City 3-1 in the Wildcard Round a year ago.

They have points in three of their last four MLS encounters but will try to snap a two-match domestic losing run at home this weekend, conceding a combined seven goals in those two defeats.

On Sunday, the Fire can beat Charlotte at home for a third consecutive occasion, having won those last two contests by a single goal.

The Crown are back in the post-season for a third successive occasion, hoping to get past round one at long last.

Dean Smith’s men set a single-season club record for goals scored in 2026 (66), averaging just under two per match (1.9) in the league this year.

This weekend, they will hope to end a four-match domestic winless run away from home and collect their first-ever road triumph in the post-season.

Defensively, they have been shaky as the visitors in 2026, conceding three or more goals on eight occasions in the regular season.

In round one of the playoffs, they have netted just one goal overall and have never scored in the opening half of an MLS road playoff game.

Charlotte have also never won a post-season game in normal time, and have scored first only once, in 2024 when they lost to Orlando City on penalties in the decisive third game of that best-of-three opening round series.

Charlotte FC Major League Soccer form:.

Due to a knock, Inter Miami loanee Noah Allen is questionable for the Fire, as is Robin Lod, who has a leg injury.

Robert Lewandowski has three goals in his last two games, netting a brace in their defeat to the Crew, with Maren Haile-Selassie also scoring on Decision Day.

On the Charlotte side, Tim Ream is questionable as he recovers from an adductor problem, Archie Goodwin may not be available due to a foot problem, Nimfasha Berchimas is recovering from foot surgery and Aron John is dealing with a shoulder injury.

Liel Abada notched a pair of goals in their regular-season finale, while a 90th-minute strike from Rodolfo Aloko earned them a point against the reigning MLS Cup champions.

Brady; Dean, Hanche-Olsen, Elliott, Gutman; Saletros, D’Avilla, Haile-Selassie; Zinckernagel, Lewandowski, Bamba.

Charlotte FC possible starting lineup:.

Kahlina; Byrne, Agyemang, Kessler, Toffolo; Diani, Westwood, Biel; De La Torre, Toklomati, Saint-Maximin.

Kevin Blackwell staying on is the right call.

Blackwell staying at the club until the end of the season doesn’t really surprise me, as there have been plenty of signs that he would be staying a lot longer than just a couple of games.

Sources indicate that the other significant development was that the owners have released an open letter on the club website. Industry observers note that in the letter, they do acknowledge that mistakes have been made, and for me, that’s a good start. But actions speak louder than words, and after so many poor decisions as of late, it will take a lot more than a letter to rebuild trust, with only time will tell whether these words are hollow or not.

In a recent development, overall, I see both announcements as a step in the right direction, as they give more clarity over the team's management and more openness from the owners.
