Mauricio Pochettino will pick his first Manchester United team on Sunday for a daunting debut away at Liverpool.

The Argentine was appointed Michael Carrick’s successor last week and only arrived in the north-west on Wednesday, leaving him just a handful of sessions to prepare his side for a crunch fixture.

It has been revealed that as such, wholesale changes from life under Carrick are not forecast, at least in terms of setup. After all, both managers have a penchant for the same 4-2-3-1 formation.

Sources indicate that carlos Baleba remains sidelined with a hamstring injury sustained against Roma in the Champions League, with Benjamin Sesko also out until the latest year, but Pochettino may well be boosted by the returns of Marcus Rashford and Luke Shaw. The latter seems the more likely of the two, with Rashford yet to be pictured in training since the international break.

Pochettino is known to be very fond of Rashford, and has reportedly attempted to sign him to other teams he has managed, meaning he can expect to get the nod if fit.

Should fit-again Shaw slot in at left-back, he may do so as one of two fresh faces in the back four. Lisandro Martinez has served his red card suspension and will be available to partner Harry Maguire, with Diogo Dalot at right-back.

A midfield pairing of Youri Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo will sit behind the trio of Matheus Cunha, Bruno Fernandes and Amad Diallo, with Bryan Mbeumo leading the line.

In a recent development, patrick Dorgu is expected to be fit, too, but it remains to be seen whether he can unseat Matheus Cunha off the left. He could also deputise Shaw if his fitness levels are not up to par.

Industry observers note that leaked drone footage of United’s Thursday training session appeared to show Pochettino working on tactics with a tight-knit group of ten outfield players, leading some to speculate that he might be dealing with Sunday’s starters. The presence of Joshua Zirkzee and Harry Amass in the group rather debunks this, though, given neither has started a Premier League match this season.

Predicted Man Utd XI vs Liverpool (4-2-3-1): Lammens; Dalot, Maguire, Martinez, Shaw; Tielemans, Mainoo; Amad, Fernandes, Cunha; Mbeumo.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Sam Varley | 19 Nov 2026 23:57.

Aiming to build a lead at the top of the League One table on the return from the international break, Huddersfield Town will welcome Leicester City to the Accu Stadium on Saturday.

The hosts currently lead second-placed Stockport County on goal difference while their visitors sit 11th and four points off the top six.

Huddersfield Town return from the November international break on Saturday aiming to pick up where they left off and pull clear at the top of the League One table.

Aiming to kick on from two disappointing years in England's third tier and fight for promotion back to the Championship, following the permanent appointment of Martin Drury over the summer, they have enjoyed an impressive campaign thus far, right now sitting top having earned 29 points from their first 14 games, winning eight and only losing one of those.

That solitary defeat came in mid-September, and the Terriers have won five and drawn two of seven league outings since, having taken on Luton Town in their final game before the break on the back of four straight victories over Plymouth Argyle, Peterborough United, Wigan Athletic and Bradford City, scoring 11 goals and conceding just two across those.

Drury's men had to settle for a point, though, levelling early in the second half through Joe Taylor in a 1-1 draw before heading into a pair of cup games, firstly bowing out of the FA Cup to fourth-tier Exeter City.

They would then beat Liverpool Under-21s 4-0 in the EFL Trophy last weekend, and now with their full focus back on League One, at the moment ahead of Stockport County on goal difference and third-placed Oxford United by three points, Huddersfield Town will hope to continue their hot streak and put another victory on the board.

Their visitors, meanwhile, return from the break with their sights set on the playoff places and the hopes of continuing an improved run of their own.

After suffering back-to-back defeats from the Premier League to League One, and turning to Russell Martin in the summer, Leicester City endured another poor start, managing just two wins and nine in their first eight games.

The Foxes appear to have turned a corner since, though, putting three more wins and a draw on the board in their last five league outings to climb into the top half, having beaten Doncaster Rovers, Bromley and Wigan Athletic alongside an away loss to Luton Town.

Martin's men then hosted Stevenage in their final league game before the break and had to settle for a point, having twice led through Sammy Braybrooke and Kamari Doyle and been pegged back, before they recorded consecutive cup victories, getting the better of Oxford City in the FA Cup and Walsall in the EFL Trophy.

Now also focused back on their League One bid, having moved within four points of the playoff spots and five of fourth place, Leicester City will hope to get back to winning ways with the scalp of the league leaders to move closer to the frontrunners on Saturday.

Huddersfield Town will remain without injured defenders Jack Whatmough and Murray Wallace and midfielders Marcus McGuane and Herbie Kane.

Drury fielded a strong team for their EFL Trophy game last week, with star forward Joe Taylor scoring another two goals to go alongside his 10 for the season in League One, and he will continue to spearhead the attack.

Derensili Sanches Fernandes will return to join him after international duty with Cape Verde, having also shone this season with seven goals and six assists in 14 League One appearances.

Leicester City have a relatively clean bill of health, other than long-term injuries for goalkeeper Jakub Stolarczyk and defender Ben Nelson.

Martin found a somewhat settle starting XI for the most part before the break, and Warren O'Hora, Harry Souttar and Caleb Okoli are bound to continue in a back three with Will Alves and Luke Thomas operating as full-backs.

Will Smallbone, John Lundstram and 18-year-old prospect Louis Page are likely left to compete for two midfield spots, while Sammy Braybrooke and Kamari Doyle may again support front man Emil Riis, who has scored six goals in nine league games so far this term, despite competition from Liam Cullen, Wes Burns and Conor Chaplin.

Huddersfield Town possible starting lineup:.

Young; Balker, Bowat, Roughan; Bronkhorst, Humphreys, Collins, Mumba; Sanches Fernandes, Taylor, Fletcher.

Leicester City possible starting lineup:.

McCarthy; O'Hora, Souttar, Okoli; Alves, Lundstram, Page, Thomas; Braybrooke, Riis, Doyle.

Leicester City certainly appear to be improving and showing their class more after a tough start, but they face a tough test away at a formidable Huddersfield Town team who also boast an abundance of quality and have settled into life under Drury perfectly.

With Taylor and Sanches Fernandes both in hot streaks, we fancy the Terriers to come out on top at home in a high-quality encounter.

Tottenham have confirmed the appointment of a latest director of women’s football, which comes as part of a thorough shake-up of the team’s management.

Kim Pedersen will take over the running of Spurs women from December 7, joining from Danish side Brondby.

He will bring to north London nearly 15 years of experience in football coaching and administration, across both the men’s and women’s game. In his most recent role, the Norwegian helped Brondby become Denmark’s first fully professional women’s outfit.

He joins a Tottenham side on something of an upward trajectory. The club has been steadily improving since the appointment of Martin Ho last year and has a clear aspiration to qualify for the Champions League, though they look set to fall short of that target this term despite heavy investment in the summer transfer window.

Pedersen’s appointment comes some six months on from the departure of the long-serving Andy Rogers, formerly managing director of the women’s team, whose 24-year spell with the club ended in May.

Speaking in an interview with the club after signing, Pedersen set his sights on helping Tottenham to upset the WSL’s heavyweights.

Also joining Tottenham women alongside Pedersen are Lucy Button, newly appointed the women’s growth director, and Hannah Sheridan, the women’s director of performance and operations.

Tottenham’s director of football operations Rafi Moersen said: “We have made a deliberate decision to evolve the way we lead Women's football at Tottenham Hotspur, establishing dedicated leadership across three critical areas: football, performance and operations, and commercial growth.

“This is about building the foundations for sustained success, on and off the pitch, with clear accountability, specialist leadership and the ambition to accelerate our progress.

“Together, these appointments, alongside continued investment in our infrastructure, represent an important step in our commitment to building a successful and sustainable future for Women's football at Tottenham Hotspur.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The footballing world was rocked earlier this month as it was announced that De Miguel had tragically passed away at the age of 30 after he was involved in a heavy collision with Andorra goalkeeper Owono.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Andorra owner Gerard Pique indicates Jesus Owono ‘does not deserve’ the 12-game suspension he received following the death of Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel.

The footballing world was rocked earlier this month as it was announced that De Miguel had tragically passed away at the age of 30 after he was involved in a heavy collision with Andorra goalkeeper Owono.

Owono had raced out of goal in the closing stages of the Spanish second-tier contest before clattering into De Miguel, whose severe head and chest injuries caused him to go into cardiac arrest.

It quickly became apparent that De Miguel required urgent medical attention and while the centre-forward’s condition was described as ‘stable but serious’ after he was carried from the field and taken to hospital, his condition quickly deteriorated – and he died the following day.

Players and organisations have united in support of De Miguel’s friends and family in the days and weeks that have followed, with heartfelt tributes shared and moments of silence observed across the globe.

Last week, Owono learned that he would be banned for Andorra’s next 12 matches for the role he played in the deadly collision, with the Spanish football federation’s disciplinary committee stating that the player had ‘violently struck an opponent in the chest with his leg, using excessive force, while the ball was in play’.

It went on: ‘The tragic outcome of the incident, resulting in the death of Jesus de Miguel Alameda, is public knowledge.

The statement added that the ‘nature of the conduct described and the accompanying circumstances’ meant that the ‘maximum sanction’ was ‘justified’.

It was also confirmed that the match involving Andorra and Tenerife – which was called off when the teams were locked at 2-2 deep into stoppage time – would not be replayed.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘This avoids having to resume play from the precise moment at which the tragic incident occurred,’ it read.

Owono’s suspension has received a mixed reaction in Spain, with some feeling it too lenient while others have called for the ‘distressed’ goalkeeper to be given greater support.

According to Andorra owner Pique, the former Barcelona, Manchester United and Spain defender, Owono is ‘not to blame’ for the tragic outcome of the deadly collision.

‘I truly believe that imposing the maximum sanction on Jesus for this action puts him in a situation he does not deserve,’ he remarked in a statement.

‘He is not to blame for all of this having happened.’.

Pique pointed to a separate incident earlier this month in Spanish football, when Albacete attacker Jose Corpas accidentally kicked Sabadell’s Quadri Liameed in the head during a second-tier encounter.

‘Fortunately Quadri is fine, the consequences in this case were not fatal, and the committee decided to sanction Corpas with three matches,’ Pique added.

‘With all this, my reflection is: what is being sanctioned, the action or the consequences?’.

Pique, a World Cup winner with Spain in 2010, made it clear that Owono would likely require a significant break away from the game before being able to compete again.

‘Jesus is going to need far more than 12 matches before he is available and able to play,’ he continued.

‘No sanction is going to bring De Miguel back to us.’.

Tenerife’s grieving squad returned to action for the first time since De Miguel’s death against Cueta on Sunday.

Goals from Nacho Gil and Neal Viereck sealed Tenerife a 2-0 victory on an emotional day the club’s Estadio Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By KIERAN GILL, MAIL SPORT REPORTER.

Published: 21:00 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 07:43 EST, 17 November 2026.

Mauricio Pochettino will have little time to waste when he takes to Manchester United's training ground for the first time on Wednesday, just days ahead of their trip to bitter rivals Liverpool.

It has been revealed that the Argentine, however, will not be doing it alone. With him, Pochettino brings to Old Trafford an experienced and familiar cast of trusted colleagues, who will be tasked with supporting him in his mission to turn things around in Manchester.

From a first-team coach who has known him since 1992 to the boss' own son, Daily Mail Sport takes a look at the backroom staff accompanying Pochettino at United...

In a recent development, when the Manchester United reporters turn up for press conferences at Carrington, they will notice one seat, usually in the front row and to the far left, has a reserved sign on it. It will be for Perez, who is Pochettino’s eyes and ears. Those same correspondents may well be followed by Perez on social media, so he can stay in the loop of what is being written.

Wherever Pochettino goes, so too does his shadow Perez. You have probably already heard about the time Pochettino met his idol Sir Alex Ferguson for lunch in London back in 2016. What you may not know is that Perez was there, too. He and Pochettino have been joined at the hip ever since they met in Barcelona when one was an analyst and the other was managing Espanyol.

Mauricio Pochettino (right) arrives at Manchester United with a trusted team of backroom staff.

That was in 2010. Perez had studied sports science at university and completed his coaching qualifications but was considering quitting football. Pochettino convinced him otherwise, and they soon learned they shared the same principles, including the importance of creating the right culture of togetherness within a club to succeed.

Sources indicate that in 2013, it was Perez’s turn to convince Pochettino. The Argentinian was unsure about moving to England to manage Southampton, but the Spaniard had spent a month on these shores studying how Premier League sides train and play.

He told Pochettino that the intensity of his sessions and style would fit perfectly and that he could not turn down the chance to take on the Premier League.

Recent findings suggest that they now consider each other family, and Perez’s story itself is a nice one. By his own admission, he will tell you he failed at becoming a professional player, but he believes the way in which he worked his way in as a coach can inspire others who dream of finding their own place in football.

He loves the game, so much so that he would use days off to travel from London to Manchester to visit the National Football Museum. Now he will be living much closer to his favourite hotspot.

As well as being the glue which connects various club departments together, Perez is a fitness and conditioning specialist, and a normal working day might involve him arriving at the training ground at 7.30am.

In a recent development, after meeting with Pochettino over breakfast, he will then hold a 9am medical meeting where aims for each player are discussed and decided. Programmes tend to be tailored to individuals rather than set for the whole squad. Perez was credited with helping to establish Southampton and Tottenham Hotspur as among the fittest teams in the Premier League.

Where Pochettino is larger than life, Perez is unassuming, and has never sought to step into management as he prefers to work in the shadows.

Jesus Perez, pictured with Pochettino at Spurs in 2019, has long been his right-hand man.

We talk about Pochettino’s man-management prowess, but the same is true of Perez.

For example, when Chelsea beat Leicester City 4-2 in an FA Cup quarter-final in 2023-24, Raheem Sterling had a stinker. He missed a penalty, spurned a one-on-one and skied a free-kick. Chelsea’s fans booed him, and chanted ‘you don’t know what you’re doing’ at Pochettino when he substituted Mykhailo Mudryk rather than Sterling after 78 minutes at 2-2. Perez was the first to go straight to Sterling to put an arm around him that day.

And when Cole Palmer was becoming a household name in Pochettino’s one and only season at Chelsea, Perez was among those who privately tried to help the Englishman understand the perils of the distractions of his latest-found fame.

When they departed Chelsea, Pochettino and Perez were men of their word and honoured their commitment to manage the World XI in the Soccer Aid charity match a few weeks later. That was despite the awkwardness of the game being held at Stamford Bridge. They lost 6-3 to Frank Lampard’s England XI.

MIGUEL D’AGOSTINO, FIRST-TEAM COACH.

To give a sense of how long Pochettino has known ‘Miki’, around 1992, Pochettino purchased his first car while a player for Newell’s Old Boys. He gave his team-mate a lift home. When D’Agostino went to get out of the car, the wind caught it hard, and broke Pochettino’s door. D'Agostino never paid the bill to have it fixed – something Pochettino occasionally likes to remind him of.

Miguel D'Agostino, known as 'Miki', has heaps of experience as a former analyst and scout.

The first-team coach has known Pochettino since 1992 (both pictured at Tottenham in 2019).

Pochettino clearly forgave his fellow defender, who was also plying his trade under Marcelo Bielsa.

It has been revealed that D’Agostino was an analyst at Espanyol, initially attached to the scouting department before assuming responsibility for filming training sessions and overseeing player analysis. From there, he followed Pochettino wherever he went, from Southampton to Tottenham to Paris Saint-Germain to Chelsea to the United States national team.

According to recent reports, while with the USA, D’Agostino would watch games in the MLS, going to Real Salt Lake or wherever there were players for scouting. In training, he is hands-on, sometimes with a stopwatch in hand or notepad containing that day’s drills.

When Pochettino tested positive for Covid-19 in January 2021, D’Agostino and Perez took temporary charge of his PSG side. They beat Angers 1-0 away from home in Ligue 1.

All of Pochettino’s confidants have a good grasp of English.

SILVIA TUYA, STRENGTH AND CONDITIONING COACH.

The newest member of Pochettino’s inner circle, having joined his USA national set-up in October 2024.

With a PhD in sports science, Tuya had worked with FC Levante Badalona in Liga F, Spain’s top tier for women’s football, while she also served as a lecturer at the National Institute of Physical Education of Catalonia at the University of Barcelona.

Since teaming up with Pochettino, she was seen on the training pitch and in the gym with the players.

Tuya will become Manchester United's first-ever female coach connected with the men's team.

Silvia Tuya is the newest member of Pochettino’s team, having joined his USA set-up in 2024.

Tuya is set to become Manchester United's first-ever female coach with the men's team.

TONI JIMENEZ, GOALKEEPING COACH.

After winning gold for Spain at the Barcelona Olympics in 1992, Jimenez met Pochettino in 1994 when they became team-mates for Espanyol, but it is worth recalling the 2000 Copa del Rey final when they found themselves on opposing sides.

It has been revealed that the goalkeeper represented Atletico Madrid, and Pochettino was in defence for Espanyol, who won 2-1. After full-time, Pochettino delayed his celebrations to go and console his friend, who had already endured a challenging year with his father having passed away.

In a recent development, jimenez has never forgotten that kindness from Pochettino, and like the others, the two have worked together wherever the latter has managed, from Espanyol to Southampton to Tottenham to PSG to Chelsea to the USA. They have shared a fair few of their favourite mate teas in their time, and now for United, where Jimenez will work with Senne Lammens and Co.

They say training is rarely boring when Jimenez is involved. He was happy to prove to Tottenham’s players during one tour of Malaysia that he could copy Rene Higuita’s scorpion kick save, for example, and is pretty good when testing his goalkeepers in free-kick practice. Lammens should beware he is liable to do a little dance if he scores past you, however.

In a recent development, hugo Lloris, the former Spurs goalkeeper who won the 2018 World Cup with France, frequently credited the charismatic Jimenez for adding upcoming areas to his game. Pochettino has also hailed Jimenez for how he keeps second and third-choice goalkeepers motivated when they are not playing.

Hugo Lloris frequently credited Toni Jimenez (pictured) for adding fresh areas to his game.

Sebastiano Pochettino first worked with his father at Tottenham (pictured celebrating at PSG).

SEBASTIANO POCHETTINO, SPORTS SCIENTIST AND FITNESS COACH.

The son of the manager. A graduate of Southampton Solent University, Sebastiano first worked with his father at Tottenham. It was said that he had become the Premier League’s youngest sports scientist when he was hired at the age of 22.

He soon became a regular sight in training sessions and on match days, seen putting the players through their paces and with the substitutes as they warmed up.

Recent findings suggest that sebastiano became a fitness coach and joined his old man at PSG, Chelsea and the USA. One of his specialties is in injury prevention, and that includes monitoring the players’ sleep and mood.

Trust is key to Pochettino, and he knows he can rely on family.

Hired by the USA as their men's national team lead analyst in August 2023 - just over a year before Pochettino took charge - Scott previously spent eight years at the FA before moving to Inter Miami.

He graduated from Liverpool John Moores University, achieving a first class BsC in Science and Football, with his major project titled 'A Comparison of the Technical Demands in Academy and Reserve Team Soccer'.

He went on to complete a PhD in Exercise Psychology & Performance Analysis there, before putting his skills to use during internships at Everton and Liverpool before joining the FA.

Scott has clearly impressed Pochettino, who confirmed before Tuesday's clash with Haiti that he was among those staying with him for that game before joining United - with Perez, Jimenez and Pochettino Jnr having travelled to England already.

It has been revealed that 'I am with Miguel and Silvia and Alec [for this game],' he said. 'After, they are going to join me in Manchester.'.

The Red Devils are set to begin their upcoming era under Mauricio Pochettino this weekend, though they face a difficult test against Liverpool at Anfield.

While many fans are hopeful that the fresh head coach can turn the club's fortunes around, starting in their next Premier League clash, they also understand that the squad he inherited is far from perfect.

It has come as no surprise to see United linked with a host of players since Pochettino's appointment, with many links being to defenders.

The i Paper claim that the Red Devils hold interest in Fulham centre-back Bassey, as well as left-back Robinson.

Man United's defence has long been questioned by supporters, with the likes of Harry Maguire and Luke Shaw into their thirties and beyond their best.

Bassey has considerable Premier League experience having played 104 Premier League games for Fulham, and the 26-year-old has so far won 64% of his duels this season.

Robinson is capable of playing excellent crosses into the penalty area, and the 29-year-old is much more mobile than Shaw.

While neither are likely to be starters in a team that wins trophies at Old Trafford, the poor physical base of the current squad must be raised, and the duo would elevate the current squad's level.

In order to play in a system as intense as Pochettino's, the players in his squad must be athletic, a quality that Robinson and Bassey share.

However, signing those two players would not address wider imbalances in the team given there are serious concerns about the likes of Lisandro Martinez and Bruno Fernandes.

Nobody should expect Pochettino to be able to solve many of United's problems in the coming weeks, but if the club want him to succeed, they must sign numerous players in the next few transfer windows.

‘He’ll use Dorgu in the short term but he’ll be one who will go in the next couple of years. Ugarte will go, 100 per cent.

‘If you look through it now I’d say Martinez would go, De Ligt would go, Mazraoui would go, Mount would go, first wave next summer. Rashford if you can, and Zirkzee.

‘And then the year after you’d be looking at Shaw, Maguire, Dalot, Bruno, that’s your second wave and maybe then you’ve made your mind up on Baleba and Santos.

‘But the earliest Mauricio Pochettino can unravel this squad is two seasons if he does well. It could take three to get this squad unravelled.’.

Bournemouth and England star Alex Scott should set his sights ‘higher’ than Chelsea and aim to join ‘one of the biggest teams in Europe’ like Arsenal.

That’s according to Chris Waddle, who claims Scott has taken his game ‘to a new level’ over the last 18 months and is looking more and more like the ‘complete’ central midfielder.

Waddle’s comments come amid mounting speculation over Scott’s future, with Bournemouth bracing themselves for incoming offers to steal their prized possession away in the January transfer window.

Scott’s eye-catching breakthrough in the international arena has done little to quieten rumours that the 23-year-old could soon be destined for bigger and better things, with Chelsea, Arsenal, Manchester City and Tottenham all rumoured to be circling.

Though Scott is right now sidelined with a thigh injury, his stock continues to soar – and it’s understood the Cherries could be prepared to do business should they receive a bid in excess of £80m this winter.

In an interview with iGaming.com, ex-England international Waddle revealed how he had been keeping close tabs on Scott’s progress since he was first alerted to his potential at Bristol City.

‘I’ve always liked Alex Scott. I think he’s a lovely, cultured player. There’s no doubt in my mind that in the last eighteen months, the kid’s taken his game to a fresh level,’ Waddle explained.

‘I followed him at Bristol City, and when he was there, I was speaking to someone that knew him who told me he was a Tottenham fan.

‘Tottenham have been collecting players in the last six months, but he is a top-class player and someone that would walk into any squad.

‘Will they move for him? It seems unlikely given the midfielders they signed in the summer.’.

Chelsea are reportedly leading the hotly contested race to sign Scott and are said to be increasingly confident of reaching an agreement with Bournemouth for the central midfielder.

However, Waddle insists Scott should ideally be aiming higher than a move to Stamford Bridge, name-checking Real Madrid, Barcelona, Bayern Munich, Paris Saint-Germain and Arsenal as potential options.

According to recent reports, ‘According to reports, Chelsea retain the strongest interest in him. No disrespect to them, but I think he can look higher. I think he’s got the ability to play for the biggest teams in Europe: Real Madrid, Barcelona, Bayern Munich, PSG, Arsenal,’ he added.

‘The guy looks like he’s a top player to me. He looks like he’s only going to get better. If I was a manager or a sporting director and I needed a midfielder, I would be looking at him.

Industry observers note that ‘He’s a complete midfielder. He can play as a 10, an 8, and a 6. He offers you a bit of everything. He reminds me a little bit of Rodri in the way that he likes to take the ball off the centre-back and start making things happen.

‘His composure and technique make him a standout player for any team looking to sign someone who can run a midfield and control the tempo.’.

While Bournemouth are in no hurry to part with Scott, the club’s hierarchy recognise that the England international may have ambitions to move on elsewhere near future.

For now, though, the Cherries are adamant that the Vitality Stadium remains the ‘right place’ for Scott.

‘At this point, we’re convinced that we’re the right place for Alex to be, for Alex to stay, and we’ll keep on addressing contract problems with Alex as we move through this year,’ Bournemouth owner Bill Foley told talkSPORT last month.

Recent findings suggest that ‘We’d love to have Alex stay here, sign a newly introduced contract and be part of this team for the long haul, and we’re still working on it. We haven’t given up.

‘But sometimes players get stars in their eyes and they think that Chelsea is the right place to go or Manchester City.’.

Scott’s current contract on the south coast runs through to June 2028.

Thierno Barry notes he has "built my confidence game by game", which has led him to believe that he can score every time he plays.

Barry joined Everton in July 2025 but struggled for form in his first campaign with the Toffees, netting just eight goals in 41 appearances across all competitions.

However, this season he has been Everton's starring man, helped by the departure of Beto to Fiorentina, which means Barry is their only out-and-out striker.

Across his first 13 games in all competitions of 2026-27, Barry has recorded 13 goal involvements (10 goals, three assists).

And in an exclusive interview with Opta Analyst, Barry noted just how important a shift in his mentality has been to hitting this rich vein of form.

"Before I joined the Premier League, I knew it was the hardest league in the world, but I didn't expect it like that!" he remarked.

"It was really hard at first. I think I needed to take my time, to really enjoy [my football here].

Sources indicate that "I think for a striker the most important thing is getting opportunities. This season, every time I play, I feel I can score a goal.

"When you feel like this, you just have to be patient; you can miss what the people might say is an 'easy' chance, but you have to switch your mind [back to the game] because you can get another chance two minutes later.

"During pre-season, I worked on my mentality, if I am feeling low, to not let it affect my game.

"For example, this season, before the game against Newcastle United, in my head I wasn't perfect because something happened in my personal life, you know?

"I came to the game and tried to do my best, even if I was feeling low, and I scored, and I think this game proved that even if I've got something going on, I can still score.".

What's your favourite Thierno Barry celebration so far? https://t.co/NAvPJ65AV2.

— Everton (@Everton) November 10, 2026.

Barry has played an instrumental part in helping Everton reach the EFL Cup quarter-finals, having netted his first hat-trick for the club against Preston North End in the second round.

But it is in the Premier League where he has really hit his stride. His six goals are the most by a player in Everton's first 10 Premier League games of a season since Dominic Calvert-Lewin in 2020-21 (10), and the most by a non-English player for the club since Romelu Lukaku in 2016-17 (seven).

The Frenchman has scored (five) or assisted (one) six of the Toffees' last seven league goals.

Only three Everton players have previously surpassed the 15-goal mark in a single Premier League season (Romelu Lukaku twice, Tony Cottee and Calvert-Lewin), and Barry is determined to make his mark in the competition.

"I appreciate these kind statistics," he told Opta Analyst of his high-scoring start to the season.

Sources indicate that "Seeing these statistics means a lot to me because I know how hard I worked [to achieve them]. I try to do my best on the pitch every game, and when it works out, it's a pleasure.

Industry observers note that "I think I've built my confidence game by game. This season, in every game, I've had an opportunity to score, and even when I miss, I know I'll have another opportunity.

"I think for a striker, the most notable thing is getting those opportunities.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Anthony Nolan | 20 Nov 2026 01:15, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 04:58.

Keen to resume their unlikely Bundesliga title challenge, Freiburg will travel to face promoted side Elversberg at Waldstadion Kaiserlinde on Saturday.

The Black and White are desperate to avoid another defeat, though Die Breisgau-Brasilianer are eyeing their fifth victory on the bounce.

Vincent Wagner's Elversberg have enjoyed an excellent beginning to their Bundesliga campaign, and have performed the best of any of the three promoted clubs this term.

Currently seventh with 13 points, the Black and White are just two points shy of sixth-placed Werder Bremen, and have fifth-placed Bayer Leverkusen within their reach this weekend.

However, Wagner's side signed off for the international break with a 2-1 loss to Borussia Dortmund at Signal Iduna Park, where they were only able to muster a late consolation via Noel Futkeu.

That defeat was to be expected on paper given the level of opposition, but the concerning factor is that it was Elversberg's third beating in four games, with the team avoiding disappointment once in a 4-1 triumph over Mainz 05 on October 30.

To make matters worse, Saturday's hosts have conceded 18 goals in nine games - a rate of two per match - the worst total in the top half of the Bundesliga.

Meanwhile, Julian Schuster's Freiburg will be vying to maintain their high-flying start to the season despite the international break disrupting their form.

Die Breisgau-Brasilianer secured a 2-0 victory over Union Berlin last time out in the league, courtesy of a second-half own goal from Rani Khedira and a follow up from Yuito Suzuki 12 minutes later.

That triumph marked a fourth in a row across all competitions for Schuster's men, who proved that their blip of three consecutive defeats in mid-October was merely a temporary stumble.

Now third with 19 points to their name, Freiburg are sitting just two points behind leaders Bayern Munich and Dortmund, and three clear of fifth-placed Leverkusen.

Though a title race is not out of the question, Champions League qualification alone would represent a major feat for Die Breisgau-Brasilianer.

With the aim of keeping ahead of their European rivals as a minimum, fans of the visitors will draw confidence from the team's attacking prowess, which has seen them score 20 goals so far - an output that has only been bettered by Bayern and RB Leipzig this season.

Elversberg form (all competitions):.

Freiburg form (all competitions):.

Elversberg will be without a number of defenders, including left-back Nicholas Mickelson, who is dealing with a medial collateral ligament injury, as well as centre-backs Lukas Pinckert and Luis Seifert, both of whom have ankle problems.

In their absence, Maximilian Rohr and Florian Le Joncour should start at the heart of Wagner's backline, flanked by Luca Sirch and Lasse Gunther.

As for Freiburg, they are missing left-back Berkay Yilmaz, who is suspended after being sent off for Freiburg II against FC-Astoria Walldorf.

That being remarked, Jordy Makengo remains available to start on the left of a four-man defence alongside Philipp Lienhart, Matthias Ginter and Philipp Treu.

Further forward, Igor Matanovic is likely to lead the line on Saturday, supported by a trio of Jan-Niklas Beste, Yuito Suzuki and Derry Scherhant.

Elversberg possible starting lineup:.

Kristof; Sirch, Rohr, Le Joncour, Gunther; Poreba, Keidel; Petkov, Onyeka, Krattenmacher; Mokwa.

Freiburg possible starting lineup:.

Backhaus; Treu, Ginter, Lienhart, Makengo; Engelhardt, Eggestein; Beste, Suzuki, Scherhant; Matanovic.

Elversberg may be lingering just outside the top six, but their defensive record suggests that they could be caught out on Saturday.

With that defensive frailty in mind, Freiburg - as one of the most potent attacking sides in the Bundesliga - will be optimistic about their chances against a team that have lost three of their last four matches.

Steely Chelsea triumph despite losing Martinez to head injury

⏱️ ~28 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • This was the afternoon when Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea went from swashbuckling to stoic, thrilling to tenacious.
  • For all Alonso’s attacking vigour at the start of his reign, there can have been no more symbolically satisfying victory under the newly introduced coach than this resolute win at Everton – the most vivid example of an increasingly impressive transformation.
  • This was what Alonso described as “winning in a different way”.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This was the afternoon when Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea went from swashbuckling to stoic, thrilling to tenacious.

For all Alonso’s attacking vigour at the start of his reign, there can have been no more symbolically satisfying victory under the newly introduced coach than this resolute win at Everton – the most vivid example of an increasingly impressive transformation.

This was what Alonso described as “winning in a different way”. A triumph amid the adversity of losing goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez to what appears to be a serious injury after a head collision with Jarrad Branthwaite is just one facet of why the joyous visiting supporters might consider this an early turning point.

Where recently they wilted, on Saturday they thrived in securing a first Premier League clean sheet for nine months.

Much more of this and the adjectives which were splattered across Chelsea during the golden years of José Mourinho – solid, robust and dogged – will be part of the Stamford Bridge lexicon once more.

Recent findings suggest that “Just one day,” Alonso warned, both acclaiming the importance of the win while wisely preaching caution. “It will be key when we manage 10 clean sheets, even though this one feels good. We need to repeat it again and again, but the mentality was very good. Sometimes it is not to play nice, it is to play good – to win second balls, and to be efficient. We needed one of these: a clean sheet and a win.”.

Asked about Martinez’s condition, Alonso said: “It was a concussion, but beyond that I do not know. I have only seen one clip of the incident, so we need to wait.

“What we know is that he left the stadium conscious and is now in hospital undergoing precautionary tests.

“We need to wait. Hopefully it will not be too serious, but at the moment we just have to wait.”.

Alonso is speedily shifting perceptions of this previously underperforming bunch, the Stamford Bridge culture on and off the pitch already unrecognisable from a few months ago.

It was Chelsea’s trip to Everton last season which facilitated the endgame of Liam Rosenior’s short, but generally hideous reign.

For those who tried to banish memories, it was a darkly comical period when Chelsea’s players were paying their respect to stationary footballs, seemingly finding new ways to stand in front of travelling fans to apologise for meek and rancid performances.

How different the scenes after Pedro Neto’s double on Merseyside – a success built on those old-fashioned and too often underestimated qualities of character and application before the artists had the final say. These are the wins that build connections and trust between players and supporters, especially during the getting-to-know-you period of a managerial tenure. While neutrals mutter about a generally disappointing spectacle, the players and supporters return home clutching three points believing they have fought together in the trenches.

Neto fires past Pickford to double Chelsea's lead! 🔥 Watch live on TNT Sports and HBO Max 📺 https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/SOJeBP5mq0.

It cannot be overlooked how this win owed a debt to the erratic refereeing of Paul Tierney, especially the amnesty he offered to Morgan Rogers on the stroke of half-time.

Already booked, Rogers was fortunate not to receive a second caution for a lunge on James Garner which took the man after the ball. A replica challenge by Everton’s Harrison Armstrong had warranted a yellow card in Tierney’s world just 21 minutes earlier.

The home team’s argument that this was a potential game changer was supported when the England midfielder was inevitably involved in the move which led to Neto breaking through 44 seconds into the second half – a lead Chelsea never looked like surrendering as Everton’s attacking limitations were exposed.

In a recent development, chelsea break the deadlock inside a minute of the second half! ⚡ Watch live on TNT Sports and HBO Max 📺 https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/E63rtGQnbv.

That should not disguise how this is a different Chelsea, contrasting not just with the characterless and rudderless team of last season, but also the defensively flawed version that began this one. Mike Penders deputised for the stricken Martínez – conscious but taken to hospital as a precaution – and was well-protected.

As much as Alonso’s artistry as a midfield maestro is presumed to define him as a coach, one cannot help but believe there are many who underestimate him as a football student. He was never going to return to England clinging to one idea given his previous Premier League experience, and he intuitively knew an away game at Everton was one for foot soldiers.

He signed Jordan Henderson for such a task. Just like his manager, the former Liverpool captain was primed for enemy territory.

Alonso’s anticipation of a fixture in which a battle had to be fought before there was an outbreak of football proved correct, aided by the fussy and generally terrible first-half officiating of Tierney.

Bizarrely, Alonso had as much cause to curse Tierney for the first of several contentious decisions, booking Armstrong for an aggressive but ultimately fair lunging challenge on Josh Acheampong. That enraged the home supporters to inspire Everton to their most dangerous spell, Thierno Barry coming closest to troubling Martínez before half-time.

Although Moisés Caicedo was denied a goal-of-the-season contender when a vicious 20-yard volley struck the crossbar, the scrappy, stop-start flavour of the occasion initially suited the hosts.

Recent findings suggest that caicedo rattles the woodwork with a stunning effort! 💥 Watch live on TNT Sports and HBO Max 📺 https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/CSIM9ogtSp.

Rogers’s reprieve changed all that. Inexplicably inconsistent as Tierney was, Chelsea exhibited a steel which thrilled Alonso as much as those games when Cole Palmer, Rogers and João Pedro are in full flow.

“They didn’t score, but did a fantastic job for the team,” Alonso pointedly mentioned of his attackers.

In a recent development, alonso’s name has not echoed so loudly across the Mersey since he played a few miles down the road from Everton’s upcoming home. After several calamitous appointments, those fans can believe their team are in safe hands again.

Thanks for reading along this afternoon.

A good win for Chelsea at Everton, but above all, let’s hope Martinez is back to full health soon.

Moyes accepted that his side had were not good enough.

He told TNT Sports: “We were a little bit unlucky with the goals. It wasn’t good defending, but it takes a couple of deflections before it gets to Neto. It makes it a relatively easy finish for him.

“The second one was a free-kick which obviously ricochets around, so I think there were parts of the game we did OK, but we didn’t offer enough to create enough, to make enough chances. I can’t think of many, so that is probably the biggest indictment.”.

He had a minor gripe over a first-half tackle that was reviewed, saying, “I think the Morgan Rogers tackle on Jimmy [Garner] could have been questioned.”.

However, given the good start to the season for Everton so far, he does not have too much rancour.

"Not as good as we wanted." 💬 David Moyes reflects on Everton's defeat to Chelsea 🔵 🎙️ @jules_breach | Watch live on TNT Sports and HBO Max 📺 https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/qPU64VjHYC.

Speaking to TNT Sports after the match, Xabi Alonso gives relatively positive news on Emi Martinez.

He describes the planned tests as “precautionary” and indicates, “as far as I know, he left the stadium conscious.”.

Neto added more detail to his thoughts on the game.

On his first goal, he explained how Everton’s defensive approach allowed them to react: “We know that they came man-to man. In the second half we adjusted some stuff. We tried to get the best of the man-to-man press and we got away. We got the cross and I could finish well, so really happy.”.

He credited his Portugal coach, Jorge Jesus, with his calmness in front of goal, adding: “This comes a little bit from the upcoming coach of the national team that says when you are near to the area you need to pass to the goal, so really happy with that.”.

According to recent reports, with Chelsea now in the Champions League places, Neto was keen to keep up the momentum. He remarked: “It’s really important. We know it’s tough to play away, even at home there are no easy games. We came here with personality, with good intentions to win the match and really happy with the result.”.

Mykhailo Mudryk has revealed that he wanted to join Arsenal.

The Tottenham winger, on loan from Chelsea, admitted that before he signed for the Blues in January 2023, he had wanted to move to north London.

He made the switch from Shakhtar Dontesk in Ukraine for an initial £61million fee, that could rise to as high as £89m.

Before he made the move to Stamford Bridge, he had been heavily linked with a move to Mikel Arteta’s side, but ultimately, he decided to join Graham Potter’s Blues instead.

Now, he has declared that his real desire was a move to Arsenal, which never materialised.

“Before going to Chelsea, I wanted to join Arsenal. It’s no secret,” he told the Ukrainian podcast ‘Guest of Gordon’.

“Arsenal were the club I wanted to play for, and moving to the Emirates Stadium was my dream.

“There weren’t even any attempts to make my dream come true and move to Arsenal.

“The attempts from my previous agent were only to earn more money.

“But at the time, I didn’t know about it. I only understood about the commission and all the rest later on.”.

Mudryk reunited with his former Shakhtar boss Roberto De Zerbi at Spurs on Deadline Day in the summer transfer window, having been cleared to play after a doping ban for meldonium which began in October 2024.

The winger made headlines on Wednesday when he blamed his country’s football association for his positive drugs test, and ex-Chelsea striker and now-president of the Ukraine FA, Andriy Shevchenko, has demanded an apology from the 25-year-old.

Mudryk played just one match for the north Londoners - away at Nottingham Forest - before suffering a “stupid” ankle injury in training, according to his manager.

He is expected to return to action this weekend, however, when Spurs take on Ipswich Town at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, looking to get back to winning ways after a 1-0 defeat at Leeds before the international break.

Xabi Alonso’s men are due to host Leeds again tomorrow (November 21) and Justin has made it clear a stern test lies ahead.

He told Premier League Studios, as quoted by the official Leeds website: “I feel like it will be a bit of a different side than what we faced in the League Cup tie, and we know they are a team that likes to play in the small spaces.

Estevao has refused to address reports linking him with a move to Paris Saint-Germain but indicates he has received ‘a lot of motivation’ during the international break having struggled for playing time at Chelsea this season.

The 19-year-old has started just one game in the Premier League this season and delivered an impressive performance in Chelsea’s 2-0 win at home to Manchester United on October 31.

However, Estevao was back on the bench for Chelsea’s 1-0 defeat to Sunderland on November 8, although he was brought on as a half-time substitute during the loss at the Stadium of Light.

Xabi Alonso praised Estevao’s response after he was left as an unused substitute during Chelsea’s penalty shootout defeat to Liverpool in the Carabao Cup last month and has insisted that the Brazilian winger ‘will have his moment’ this season.

However, reports have claimed that Estevao has been unhappy with his lack of playing time under Alonso and is considering his future at Chelsea.

Estevao started in both of Brazil’s friendlies during the international break and delivered a lively display during the 7-0 win over Singapore on Tuesday as he scored a goal and registered two assists.

‘I’m very happy to have received the minutes in the friendlies,’ Estevao told ESPN Brasil after his national side’s win at the National Stadium in Singapore.

‘I thank Ancelotti for his confidence because every player wants to play and at Chelsea I’ve had few minutes, but coming here and knowing that the manager trusts me gives me a lot of motivation.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Brighton & Hove Albion owner Tony Bloom has claimed that Fabian Hurzeler supports Bayern Munich and could move there in the future.
  • The Seagulls have been the surprise package of the Premier League season, with the club right now in second place after 10 matchweeks.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Nolan | 20 Nov 2026 02:21.

Brighton & Hove Albion owner Tony Bloom has claimed that Fabian Hurzeler supports Bayern Munich and could move there in the future.

The Seagulls have been the surprise package of the Premier League season, with the club right now in second place after 10 matchweeks.

Few could have predicted that they would also be the division's top scorers (26), and the team's form has led to universal praise for boss Hurzeler.

The German head coach has understandably been linked with a number of sides in the league, including Manchester United, though the Red Devils have appointed Mauricio Pochettino as Michael Carrick's replacement.

Speaking to reporters, Brighton owner Bloom insisted that he intends to keep Hurzeler at the club for a long time, though admitted that Bayern Munich could tempt the manager, saying: "Fabian is doing an unbelievable job. He is really enjoying it here and we would fight ridiculously hard to keep him if we had to.

"I don’t think he is going anywhere for a long time and we are just enjoying the ride. He is improving. We have given him the facilities, the players, the set-up to really grow as a head coach and he is taking that opportunity. We are very fortunate to have him and long may that continue.

"He will be at the top or near the top of the [list for the] best clubs in the world when they need to hire, but he’s young. He can go to these substantial clubs down the road [time-wise]. [Bayern Munich] is his team. I am sure he will be head coach of Bayern Munich at some time probably.".

Brighton are in a much stronger position than 18th-placed United, so it would make sense if Hurzeler was reluctant about potentially joining them in favour of a more stable team Bayern.

While Hurzeler may be the brightest prospect in management, Premier League clubs may find it difficult to appoint him in the coming years.

United have only just appointed Pochettino, so they will almost certainly spend considerable time and resources on the Argentine.

Arsenal are likely to keep Mikel Arteta for a number of seasons, while Manchester City could be demoted to lower divisions.

Liverpool are embarking upon their first campaign under Andoni Iraola, and it would be extraordinary if they sacked him after one season.

Chelsea have never been afraid to sack a head coach, so Xabi Alonso's position should not necessarily be seen as secure, but the Spaniard is highly regarded by many.

Given Bayern Munich currently employ Vincent Kompany, the Bavarians may not be in the market for a fresh head coach for a considerable period.

That could have left an opening for United to approach Brighton for Hurzeler, though it is far too early to suggest that the Red Devils have made a mistake by not trying to appoint the 33-year-old.

The club are in the relegation zone, and convincing Brighton to part with Hurzeler may have been impossible, especially as the Seagulls could realistically qualify for the Champions League.

Hiring an interim boss could have deepened United's relegation woes, and of the managers available in November, there were few with the pedigree of Pochettino.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

England will face Norway in the Nations League quarter-finals, and they could lock horns with a familiar foe in the last four should they make it.

It will be the first time that Thomas Tuchel’s side have played the Scandinavians since the World Cup quarter-finals, where England won out 2-1 in Miami, Florida thanks to a brace from Jude Bellingham after Andreas Schjelderup’s stunning opener.

The Three Lions found out their opponents in Friday’s knockout-stage draw, which took place at UEFA’s headquarters in Nyon, Switzerland.

Tuchel’s men finished top of Group A after a stunning 3-2 victory over world champions Spain in Madrid last weekend.

Luis de la Fuente’s European champions, meanwhile, will take on France in their last-eight clash, with the European giants set to face off for the first time since the World Cup semi-final, where La Roja emerged 2-0 winners thanks to Mikel Oyarzabal and Pedro Porro’s goals.

The remaining two fixtures are the Netherlands against Portugal, and Belgium facing Germany.

The four quarter-finals will take place in March next year, with the winners going through to the finals in June next year.

The semi-finals were also revealed, with England on a collision course with historic rivals Germany, should the Three Lions get through Norway and Jurgen Klopp’s men beat Belgium.

The victors of Spain vs France will take on the winners between the Netherlands and Portugal.

Netherlands/Portugal vs Spain/France.

Norway/England vs Belgium/Germany.

Published: 05:25 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 08:02 EST, 17 November 2026.

Tony Mowbray has stepped down from his role as Blackburn Rovers manager due to ill health.

The 62-year-old, who previously had to walk away from his job at Birmingham City in 2024 due to a battle with bowel cancer, leaves Blackburn with immediate effect.

The Championship side declared his departure with a statement from Mowbray. It read: 'Unfortunately, due to health issues, I have to step back from my role as Head Coach of Blackburn Rovers.

In a recent development, 'I’m immensely proud of this group of players. Their dedication and professionalism have given us some memorable performances and wins, and I’ve loved working with them.

It has been revealed that 'Thank you to my coaching staff for all your hard work and for the support you’ve given me. It’s been a pleasure working alongside you.

'To the fans, thank you for the way you’ve supported me and the team this season. I’ve always tried to give you a team that you can be proud of. Your support has meant a great deal to me.

Tony Mowbray has stepped down from his role as Blackburn Rovers boss due to ill health.

'I’m grateful to the Owners and Suhail (Pasha, chief operating officer) for giving me the opportunity to lead this great club once again.

Sources indicate that 'I’d ask that you give me and my family privacy at this time. Thank you for your understanding.'.

Mowbray leaves with Blackburn 13th in the Championship. He took over at the club in June this year having spent two years out of the game following his health issues at Birmingham City.

The veteran manager suddenly stepped down as manager of Birmingham in February 2024 after undergoing surgery for bowel cancer. He had 15cm of his bowel removed during his treatment.

He took a temporary leave of absence after eight games in charge, before officially resigning from the role in May.

Mowbray, who has managed a host of English clubs, opened up publicly about his struggles, telling the Times that his children had feared the worst.

'I had the conversation with my family and you could see they were frightened,' he remarked. 'Was I frightened? My only thoughts were for my family, my three children and my wife and making sure they were OK.

Recent findings suggest that 'I had to put everything in order and I tried to. My wife saw our banking app for the first time in her life. It's little things like that. She understood. This was serious stuff. I felt she needed to know where we had our money, whether it was ISAs or pensions and what was in the bank.'.

Speaking on his diagnosis, which came after he collapsed when trying to answer the door, he added: 'My wife put me in the car and drove me back to hospital and they wanted to know why I was collapsing and in the condition I was,' he says. 'They rehydrated me and put me on a drip overnight.

In a recent development, 'I remember sitting there in bed and my kids' eyes were watering up. They were scared I wasn't going to live. How old were they? They were 15, 17 and 19. I could see the fear in their eyes.'.

Mowbray's comeback story when he was made Blackburn boss in the summer was one of the feel-good moments of the offseason. It has not been disclosed what his current health issue is.

Mowbray leaves Blackburn with the team in 13th place in the Championship table.

Blackburn Rovers owner Balaji Rao added his own statement, writing: 'Our thoughts are with Tony and his family as he steps back from his duties to focus on his health.

'Through our many meetings over the years, we’ve come to know Tony well and grown very fond of him. We’ve always admired his professionalism, his dedication and the passion he brings to his work at Blackburn Rovers.

It has been revealed that 'Tony, please know that you have our unconditional and unwavering support. We send you and your family our love and strength, and we will do all we can to support you through this time.'.

Chief Executive Officer Steve Curwood stated: 'Tony’s passion for the club and his professionalism are clear to see, but it is his kindness and the care he shows for players, staff and those around him that mean so much.

'Our priority now is to make sure he feels that same care and support from all of us. We will support him and his family in every way we can.

'On behalf of everyone at Blackburn Rovers, I would like to send Tony and his family our very best wishes during this time.'.

A look at how Barnsley and Sheffield Wednesday could line up for their South Yorkshire derby clash.

Barnsley and Sheffield Wednesday are set to do battle in a South Yorkshire derby under the Oakwell lights.

The former are languishing in the League One relegation zone, while the latter are sitting fifth and aiming to break into the top two.

Wednesday will be fancied to claim three points at the expense of their neighbours and rivals, but form does tend to go out of the window in derbies.

In a recent development, barnsley boss Daniel Stendel noted: “What I would like is that we have a big support in the game. Not just because it's a derby but also these young guys, without the captain (Cameron McGeehan), need the push from the stands.”.

There are plenty of subplots heading into the fixture and one of them concerns Davis Keillor-Dunn. The 28-year-old was a talismanic figure at the top end of the pitch for Barnsley and could face them tonight in the colours of Wednesday.
